मणिप्रवरसोपानां मुक्तासिकतशोभिताम्

kṛtrimāṁ dīrghikāṁ cāpi pūrṇāṁ śītena vāriṇā
maṇipravarasopānāṁ muktāsikataśobhitām
He saw a big artificial pond full of cool water having stairs crusted with excellent jewels and its sandy banks filled with pearls.

विविधैर्मृगसंघैश्च विचित्रां चित्रकाननाम्
प्रासादैः सुमहद्भिश्च निर्मितैर्विश्वकर्मणा
काननैः कृत्रिमैश्चापि सर्वतः समलंकृताम्

vividhairmṛgasaṁghaiśca vicitrāṁ citrakānanām
prāsādaiḥ sumahadbhiśca nirmitairviśvakarmaṇā
kānanaiḥ kṛtrimaiścāpi sarvataḥ samalaṁkṛtām

It was embellished on all sides) with various animals, diverse trees and big mansions made by Visvakarmat himself. It was adorned all around with artificial forests and all the trees there bore flowers and fruits, spreading their branches like to umbrellas and having golden and silvern pavements under them. 'The son of Brahma and artist of gods.

लताप्रतानैर्बहुभिः पर्णैश्च बहुभिर्वृताम्
काञ्चनीं शिंशुपामेकां ददर्श स महाकपिः

latāpratānairbahubhiḥ parṇaiśca bahubhirvṛtām
kāñcanīṁ śiṁśupāmekāṁ dadarśa sa mahākapiḥ
And that great monkey beheld there one golden Singsapa* tree surrounded on all sides with golden pavements. 'A tree (Dalbergia Sisu).

सोऽपश्यद्भूमिभागांश्च गर्तप्रस्रवणानि च
सुवर्णवृक्षानपरान्ददर्श शिखिसंनिभान्

so'paśyadbhūmibhāgāṁśca gartaprasravaṇāni ca
suvarṇavṛkṣānaparāndadarśa śikhisaṁnibhān
And he saw the glebe, the hill streams and many a golden trees resembling the fire.

तेषां द्रुमाणां प्रभया मेरोरिव महाकपिः
अमन्यत तदा वीरः काञ्चनोऽस्मीति वानरः

teṣāṁ drumāṇāṁ prabhayā meroriva mahākapiḥ
amanyata tadā vīraḥ kāñcano'smīti vānaraḥ
By the lustre of all those trees that heroic monkey appeared as if made of gold like to the Sun by the touch of the mount Sumeru.

तां काञ्चनैस्तरुगणैर्मारुतेन च वीजिताम्
किङ्किणीशतनिर्घोषां दृष्ट्वा विस्मयमागमत्

tāṁ kāñcanaistarugaṇairmārutena ca vījitām
kiṅkiṇīśatanirghoṣāṁ dṛṣṭvā vismayamāgamat
Having seen those beautiful golden trees, shaken by the wind and making a sound like that of a Kinkini; having flowery tops and new leaves he was greatly amazed.

इतो द्रक्ष्यामि वैदेहीं राम दर्शनलालसाम्
इतश्चेतश्च दुःखार्तां संपतन्तीं यदृच्छया

ito drakṣyāmi vaidehīṁ rāma darśanalālasām
itaścetaśca duḥkhārtāṁ saṁpatantīṁ yadṛcchayā

And climbing that Singsapa tree enveloped with leaves that monkey, gifted with velocity, reflected— Perchance I may see Vaidehi, exercised with grief, anxious to behold Rama and wandering hither and thither at her pleasure.

अशोकवनिका चेयं दृढं रम्या दुरात्मनः
चम्पकैश्चन्दनैश्चापि बकुलैश्च विभूषिता

aśokavanikā ceyaṁ dṛḍhaṁ ramyā durātmanaḥ
campakaiścandanaiścāpi bakulaiśca vibhūṣitā

Certainly this is the picturesque Asoka forest of that vicious-souled one, embellished with sandal Champakas and Bakulas. Here is a beautiful pond abounding in lotuses, thronged with birds and forsooth shall that royal spouse Janaki repair hither.

अथ वा मृगशावाक्षी वनस्यास्य विचक्षणा
वनमेष्यति सा चेह रामचिन्तानुकर्शिता

atha vā mṛgaśāvākṣī vanasyāsya vicakṣaṇā
vanameṣyati sā ceha rāmacintānukarśitā

She is the beloved queen of Raghava and expert in walking in the garden. And separated from Rama, certainly shall Janaki repair hither. Or she having the eyes of a young antelope and adept in roaming in the forest, exercised with thought touching Rama, shall come here.

रामशोकाभिसंतप्ता सा देवी वामलोचना
वनवासरता नित्यमेष्यते वनचारिणी

rāmaśokābhisaṁtaptā sā devī vāmalocanā
vanavāsaratā nityameṣyate vanacāriṇī

Or she having beautiful eyes and fond of ranging in the forest, racked with sorrow in consequence of Rama's separation, dose always frequent this forest.* *The commentator, Ramanuja interprets this bloka as explaining the cause of Sita's frequenting the Asoka forest.

वनेचराणां सततं नूनं स्पृहयते पुरा
रामस्य दयिता भार्या जनकस्य सुता सती

vanecarāṇāṁ satataṁ nūnaṁ spṛhayate purā
rāmasya dayitā bhāryā janakasya sutā satī
Ere this, the chaste and worshipful spouse of Rama–Janaka's daughter, used to love always the birds and animals of the forest.

संध्याकालमनाः श्यामा ध्रुवमेष्यति जानकी
नदीं चेमां शिवजलां संध्यार्थे वरवर्णिनी

saṁdhyākālamanāḥ śyāmā dhruvameṣyati jānakī
nadīṁ cemāṁ śivajalāṁ saṁdhyārthe varavarṇinī

(The morning has set in) and surely the beautiful and graceful daughter of Janaka fond of performing morning ablutions, shall come to this river of pure water to perform them. "Sandhya literally means the point of time which connect day and night. It however, generally means the period after sunset and before the night sets. But here with reference to the speech which Hanuman began by the end of night, it means the morning.

तस्याश्चाप्यनुरूपेयमशोकवनिका शुभा
शुभा या पार्थिवेन्द्रस्य पत्नी रामस्य संमिता

tasyāścāpyanurūpeyamaśokavanikā śubhā
śubhā yā pārthivendrasya patnī rāmasya saṁmitā
Truly is this beautiful forest of Asoka the worthy abode of the beloved and chaste spouse of Rama, the lord of men.

यदि जिवति सा देवी ताराधिपनिभानना
आगमिष्यति सावश्यमिमां शिवजलां नदीम्

yadi jivati sā devī tārādhipanibhānanā
āgamiṣyati sāvaśyamimāṁ śivajalāṁ nadīm
If that one of moon-like countenance breathes forsooth shall she come to this river of cool water."

एवं तु मत्वा हनुमान्महात्मा; प्रतीक्षमाणो मनुजेन्द्रपत्नीम्
अवेक्षमाणश्च ददर्श सर्वं; सुपुष्पिते पर्णघने निलीनः

evaṁ tu matvā hanumānmahātmā; pratīkṣamāṇo manujendrapatnīm
avekṣamāṇaśca dadarśa sarvaṁ; supuṣpite parṇaghane nilīnaḥ

Having arrived there and anxiously expecting the appearance of the spouse of that lord of men, the high-souled Hanuman hiding himself (on the Singsapa tree) enveloped with flowers and leaves, beheld all.

स वीक्षमाणस्तत्रस्थो मार्गमाणश्च मैथिलीम्
अवेक्षमाणश्च महीं सर्वां तामन्ववैक्षत

sa vīkṣamāṇastatrastho mārgamāṇaśca maithilīm
avekṣamāṇaśca mahīṁ sarvāṁ tāmanvavaikṣata
Having stationed himself on the tree, casting his looks all around in quest of Sita and looking down on the carth he surveyed the entire forest of (Asoka).

सन्तान कलताभिश्च पादपैरुपशोभिताम्
दिव्यगन्धरसोपेतां सर्वतः समलंकृताम्

santāna kalatābhiśca pādapairupaśobhitām
divyagandharasopetāṁ sarvataḥ samalaṁkṛtām
It was beautified with Santdaka creepers and various trees, fragrant with celestial odours and was embellished on all sides.

सर्वर्तुकुसुमै रम्यैः फलवद्भिश्च पादपैः
पुष्पितानामशोकानां श्रिया सूर्योदयप्रभाम्

sarvartukusumai ramyaiḥ phalavadbhiśca pādapaiḥ
puṣpitānāmaśokānāṁ śriyā sūryodayaprabhām

It resembled Nandana or the celestial garden, and was filled with various animals and birds, palaces and mansions; resounded with the notes of Kokilas; adorned with the ponds abounding in silvern water-lilies and lotuses; filled with many seats and coverlets and various houses having spacious courtyards; adorned with beautiful flowers of all seasons and trees bearing fruits. And the beauty of the blossoming Asokas resembled the effulgence of the Sun.

प्रदीप्तामिव तत्रस्थो मारुतिः समुदैक्षत
निष्पत्रशाखां विहगैः क्रियमाणामिवासकृत्
विनिष्पतद्भिः शतशश्चित्रैः पुष्पावतंसकैः

pradīptāmiva tatrastho mārutiḥ samudaikṣata
niṣpatraśākhāṁ vihagaiḥ kriyamāṇāmivāsakṛt
viniṣpatadbhiḥ śataśaścitraiḥ puṣpāvataṁsakaiḥ
And stationed there Maruti beheld trees as if devoid of leaves on account of the hundreds of birds, adorned with various flowers, resorting there.

कर्णिकारैः कुसुमितैः किंशुकैश्च सुपुष्पितैः
स देशः प्रभया तेषां प्रदीप्त इव सर्वतः

karṇikāraiḥ kusumitaiḥ kiṁśukaiśca supuṣpitaiḥ
sa deśaḥ prabhayā teṣāṁ pradīpta iva sarvataḥ

He saw there the earth touched by Asoka trees, the removers of grief, having flowers growing from the roots and lowered down with their weight. And the entire quarter was as if ablaze with the beauty of the flowery Karrikaras and Kingsukas.

पुंनागाः सप्तपर्णाश्च चम्पकोद्दालकास्तथा
विवृद्धमूला बहवः शोभन्ते स्म सुपुष्पिताः

puṁnāgāḥ saptaparṇāśca campakoddālakāstathā
vivṛddhamūlā bahavaḥ śobhante sma supuṣpitāḥ
There appeared in beauty many-flowery Punnagas, Saptaparnas, Champakas, and Udalakas having deeply expanded roots.

शातकुम्भनिभाः केचित्केचिदग्निशिखोपमाः
नीलाञ्जननिभाः केचित्तत्राशोकाः सहस्रशः

śātakumbhanibhāḥ kecitkecidagniśikhopamāḥ
nīlāñjananibhāḥ kecittatrāśokāḥ sahasraśaḥ
And there was a thousand of Asoka trees, some of whom were like gold, some were like the flame of fire and some were like dark-blue collyrium.

नन्दनं विविधोद्यानं चित्रं चैत्ररथं यथा
अतिवृत्तमिवाचिन्त्यं दिव्यं रम्यं श्रिया वृतम्

nandanaṁ vividhodyānaṁ citraṁ caitrarathaṁ yathā
ativṛttamivācintyaṁ divyaṁ ramyaṁ śriyā vṛtam
It was like the garden of Nandana or like that of Kubera or perhaps it surpassed the both in excellence.

द्वितीयमिव चाकाशं पुष्पज्योतिर्गणायुतम्
पुष्परत्नशतैश्चित्रं पञ्चमं सागरं यथा

dvitīyamiva cākāśaṁ puṣpajyotirgaṇāyutam
puṣparatnaśataiścitraṁ pañcamaṁ sāgaraṁ yathā

Enveloped in charming, celestial grace beyond conception and having flowers for stars that forest appeared like a second sky, And covered with hundreds of pearl-like flowers the forest looked like the fifth ocean.

सर्वर्तुपुष्पैर्निचितं पादपैर्मधुगन्धिभिः
नानानिनादैरुद्यानं रम्यं मृगगणैर्द्विजैः

sarvartupuṣpairnicitaṁ pādapairmadhugandhibhiḥ
nānāninādairudyānaṁ ramyaṁ mṛgagaṇairdvijaiḥ

And that garden was embellished with flowers of all seasons and honey-smelling trees, and filled with diverse notes and various animals and birds. And that fragrant garden was rendered more charming with various other fragrances. And that foremost of monkeys beheld in that garden of Asoka, a round palace, situated at a distance, fragrantas the Gandhamadana mountain and high as the lord of mountains.

ततो मलिनसंवीतां राक्षसीभिः समावृताम्
उपवासकृशां दीनां निःश्वसान्तीं पुनः पुनः
ददर्श शुक्लपक्षादौ चन्द्ररेखामिवामलाम्

tato malinasaṁvītāṁ rākṣasībhiḥ samāvṛtām
upavāsakṛśāṁ dīnāṁ niḥśvasāntīṁ punaḥ punaḥ
dadarśa śuklapakṣādau candrarekhāmivāmalām

Thereupon he beheld there (Sita) wearing a soiled cloth, poorly, greatly reduced by fast, sighing again and again and encircled by a band of Raksasis. She was (however) spotless like to the rays of the moon on the first lunar day.

मन्दप्रख्यायमानेन रूपेण रुचिरप्रभाम्
पिनद्धां धूमजालेन शिखामिव विभावसोः

mandaprakhyāyamānena rūpeṇa ruciraprabhām
pinaddhāṁ dhūmajālena śikhāmiva vibhāvasoḥ
Her graceful beauty could with great difficulty be perceived lie to the flame of fire enveloped with smoke.

पीतेनैकेन संवीतां क्लिष्टेनोत्तमवाससा
सपङ्कामनलंकारां विपद्मामिव पद्मिनीम्

pītenaikena saṁvītāṁ kliṣṭenottamavāsasā
sapaṅkāmanalaṁkārāṁ vipadmāmiva padminīm

And wearing a shattered and soiled yellow cloth and divested of all ornaments she appeared like a lotus stalk without lotuses.* *This passage has another meaning-Padmini has two meanings— (i) lotus (ii) Laksmi or the goddess of wealth. The goddess of wealth is generally described as sitting on a lotus.

व्रीडितां दुःखसंतप्तां परिम्लानां तपस्विनीम्
ग्रहेणाङ्गारकेणैव पीडितामिव रोहिणीम्

vrīḍitāṁ duḥkhasaṁtaptāṁ parimlānāṁ tapasvinīm
graheṇāṅgārakeṇaiva pīḍitāmiva rohiṇīm
Oppressed, racked with grief, weakened and chaste as she was, she appeared like Rohini possessed by Ketu.

अश्रुपूर्णमुखीं दीनां कृशामननशेन च
शोकध्यानपरां दीनां नित्यं दुःखपरायणाम्

aśrupūrṇamukhīṁ dīnāṁ kṛśāmananaśena ca
śokadhyānaparāṁ dīnāṁ nityaṁ duḥkhaparāyaṇām
She was greatly reduced by fast, stricken with grief and anxious thoughts, disturbed with sorrow and was poorly and her eyes were always full of tears.

प्रियं जनमपश्यन्तीं पश्यन्तीं राक्षसीगणम्
स्वगणेन मृगीं हीनां श्वगणाभिवृतामिव

priyaṁ janamapaśyantīṁ paśyantīṁ rākṣasīgaṇam
svagaṇena mṛgīṁ hīnāṁ śvagaṇābhivṛtāmiva

Separated from her kith and kin and not beholding Rama and Laksmana* but the Raks asis, she appeared like a hind surrounded by dogs. *Priyajanam-literally means dear ones—but here it refers to Rama and Laksmana.

नीलनागाभया वेण्या जघनं गतयैकया
सुखार्हां दुःखसंतप्तां व्यसनानामकोदिवाम्

nīlanāgābhayā veṇyā jaghanaṁ gatayaikayā
sukhārhāṁ duḥkhasaṁtaptāṁ vyasanānāmakodivām
Her braid of long hair resembling a black serpent falling on her back it appeared as if the Earth was filled with dark-blue forests on the disappearance of the rains.

तां समीक्ष्य विशालाक्षीमधिकं मलिनां कृशाम्
तर्कयामास सीतेति कारणैरुपपादिभिः

tāṁ samīkṣya viśālākṣīmadhikaṁ malināṁ kṛśām
tarkayāmāsa sīteti kāraṇairupapādibhiḥ

She was worthy of happiness only and never knew of misery and therefore she was (now) greatly oppressed with sorrow. And beholding that one of expansive eyes rendered pale and feeble, Hanuman, Hanuman, by various conclusive arguments reflected within himself. She must be Sita for this damsel looks just like her, whom I saw, when she was ravished by Ravana, assuming shapes at will.

पूर्णचन्द्राननां सुभ्रूं चारुवृत्तपयोधराम्
कुर्वन्तीं प्रभया देवीं सर्वा वितिमिरा दिशः

pūrṇacandrānanāṁ subhrūṁ cāruvṛttapayodharām
kurvantīṁ prabhayā devīṁ sarvā vitimirā diśaḥ

Having the countenance of the full-moon, beautiful eye brows, round breast, she is as if dispelling the darkness from all quarters by virtue of her grace. Her throat was yellow, and her lips were like Bimbas.* She was of middle stature and her limbs were all well built. *A circubituceous plant with red fruits.

इष्टां सर्वस्य जगतः पूर्णचन्द्रप्रभामिव
भूमौ सुतनुमासीनां नियतामिव तापसीम्

iṣṭāṁ sarvasya jagataḥ pūrṇacandraprabhāmiva
bhūmau sutanumāsīnāṁ niyatāmiva tāpasīm

She had eyes resembling lotus petals and was like the beloved wife of Manmatha-Rati and was adorable to the whole creation like the rays of the full-moon. That one having a graceful person was seated on the earth like a female ascetic having her senses restrained. And she was sighing again and again like the timid daughterin-law of the lord of serpents.* *The epithet has a special significance because through her the destruction of the race of Raksasas was brought about.

निःश्वासबहुलां भीरुं भुजगेन्द्रवधूमिव
शोकजालेन महता विततेन न राजतीम्

niḥśvāsabahulāṁ bhīruṁ bhujagendravadhūmiva
śokajālena mahatā vitatena na rājatīm
Entangled by a mighty web of grief her grace was greatly lessened and she appeared like the flame of fire enveloped in smoke.

विहतामिव च श्रद्धामाशां प्रतिहतामिव
सोपसर्गां यथा सिद्धिं बुद्धिं सकलुषामिव

vihatāmiva ca śraddhāmāśāṁ pratihatāmiva
sopasargāṁ yathā siddhiṁ buddhiṁ sakaluṣāmiva
She was like to Smrti of doubtful meanings, fallen wealth, lost respect, hope without any desire for gain, Siddhis of many troubles, sullied understanding and fame soiled with false rumours.

अबलां मृगशावाक्षीं वीक्षमाणां ततस्ततः
बाष्पाम्बुप्रतिपूर्णेन कृष्णवक्त्राक्षिपक्ष्मणा
वदनेनाप्रसन्नेन निःश्वसन्तीं पुनः पुनः

abalāṁ mṛgaśāvākṣīṁ vīkṣamāṇāṁ tatastataḥ
bāṣpāmbupratipūrṇena kṛṣṇavaktrākṣipakṣmaṇā
vadanenāprasannena niḥśvasantīṁ punaḥ punaḥ
With a displeased countenance, having darkblue and curling eye lashes, and eyes full of tears, she was sighing again and again.

मलपङ्कधरां दीनां मण्डनार्हाममण्डिताम्
प्रभां नक्षत्रराजस्य कालमेघैरिवावृताम्

malapaṅkadharāṁ dīnāṁ maṇḍanārhāmamaṇḍitām
prabhāṁ nakṣatrarājasya kālameghairivāvṛtām

Worthy of Wearing ornaments but now without any, poorly, crusted with execrations, she appeared like the rays of the stars enveloped by dark-blue clouds. And beholding Sita in that pitiable plight like to learning for want of practice, (Hanuman) was Puzzled with doubts.

दुःखेन बुबुधे सीतां हनुमाननलंकृताम्
संस्कारेण यथाहीनां वाचमर्थान्तरं गताम्

duḥkhena bubudhe sītāṁ hanumānanalaṁkṛtām
saṁskāreṇa yathāhīnāṁ vācamarthāntaraṁ gatām
Seeing her without ornaments he could with great difficulty make her out like to words having different meanings without the knowledge of grammar.

तां समीक्ष्य विशालाक्षीं राजपुत्रीमनिन्दिताम्
तर्कयामास सीतेति कारणैरुपपादयन्

tāṁ samīkṣya viśālākṣīṁ rājaputrīmaninditām
tarkayāmāsa sīteti kāraṇairupapādayan
And beholding that blameless daughter of the king, having expansive eyes, Hanuman, by various reasonings, reflected-“Forsooth she must be Sita."

वैदेह्या यानि चाङ्गेषु तदा रामोऽन्वकीर्तयत्
तान्याभरणजालानि गात्रशोभीन्यलक्षयत्

vaidehyā yāni cāṅgeṣu tadā rāmo'nvakīrtayat
tānyābharaṇajālāni gātraśobhīnyalakṣayat
I see at her person all these ornaments, of which Rama mentioned to me at the time of my departure.

सुकृतौ कर्णवेष्टौ च श्वदंष्ट्रौ च सुसंस्थितौ
मणिविद्रुमचित्राणि हस्तेष्वाभरणानि च

sukṛtau karṇaveṣṭau ca śvadaṁṣṭrau ca susaṁsthitau
maṇividrumacitrāṇi hasteṣvābharaṇāni ca
I behold on her ears excellent ear-rings and nicely placed Svadangstras and on her arms jewelled ornaments rendered dark-blue by dirt for constant use.

श्यामानि चिरयुक्तत्वात्तथा संस्थानवन्ति च
तान्येवैतानि मन्येऽहं यानि रामोऽव्नकीर्तयत्

śyāmāni cirayuktatvāttathā saṁsthānavanti ca
tānyevaitāni manye'haṁ yāni rāmo'vnakīrtayat
Verily these are the ornaments Rama mentioned to me. I do not perceive them which had been cast off by her. But these are the rest there is not the least doubt about it.

भूषणानि च मुख्यानि दृष्टानि धरणीतले
अनयैवापविद्धानि स्वनवन्ति महान्ति च

bhūṣaṇāni ca mukhyāni dṛṣṭāni dharaṇītale
anayaivāpaviddhāni svanavanti mahānti ca
The monkeys had seen, her excellent yellow cloth made of golden fibres, on the hill. They had seen also her excellent ornaments, which cast off by her, fell on the earth with a sound.

इदं चिरगृहीतत्वाद्वसनं क्लिष्टवत्तरम्
तथा हि नूनं तद्वर्णं तथा श्रीमद्यथेतरत्

idaṁ ciragṛhītatvādvasanaṁ kliṣṭavattaram
tathā hi nūnaṁ tadvarṇaṁ tathā śrīmadyathetarat
Her cloth has been shattered by constant use but her grace has not been rendered worse than its colour.

इयं कनकवर्णाङ्गी रामस्य महिषी प्रिया
प्रनष्टापि सती यस्य मनसो न प्रणश्यति

iyaṁ kanakavarṇāṅgī rāmasya mahiṣī priyā
pranaṣṭāpi satī yasya manaso na praṇaśyati
This one having a golden countenance must be the beloved queen of Rama who, albeit separated from him, has not disappeared from his mind.

स्त्री प्रनष्टेति कारुण्यादाश्रितेत्यानृशंस्यतः
पत्नी नष्टेति शोकेन प्रियेति मदनेन च

strī pranaṣṭeti kāruṇyādāśritetyānṛśaṁsyataḥ
patnī naṣṭeti śokena priyeti madanena ca

This is that damsel on whose account Rama being simultaneously burnt by affection, pity, grief and amour, affection in consequence of his beloved spouse being ravished, pity for his inability to protect one dependent on him, grief for the loss of his beloved wife and amour for his dear one.

अस्या देव्या यथा रूपमङ्गप्रत्यङ्गसौष्ठवम्
रामस्य च यथारूपं तस्येयमसितेक्षणा

asyā devyā yathā rūpamaṅgapratyaṅgasauṣṭhavam
rāmasya ca yathārūpaṁ tasyeyamasitekṣaṇā
Verily it appear from the grace of her person, from her well developed limbs and from Rama's beauty that this worshipful damsel having darkblue eyes must be his spouse.

अस्या देव्या मनस्तस्मिंस्तस्य चास्यां प्रतिष्ठितम्
तेनेयं स च धर्मात्मा मुहूर्तमपि जीवति

asyā devyā manastasmiṁstasya cāsyāṁ pratiṣṭhitam
teneyaṁ sa ca dharmātmā muhūrtamapi jīvati
She has her mind fixed in him, and he in her and it is for this that she and the virtuous-souled (Rama) have been still maintaining their being.

एवं सीतां तदा दृष्ट्वा हृष्टः पवनसंभवः
जगाम मनसा रामं प्रशशंस च तं प्रभुम्

evaṁ sītāṁ tadā dṛṣṭvā hṛṣṭaḥ pavanasaṁbhavaḥ
jagāma manasā rāmaṁ praśaśaṁsa ca taṁ prabhum
Having beheld Sita in this plight, that son of the wind-god approached Rama in mind and showered praises on his master.

प्रशस्य तु प्रशस्तव्यां सीतां तां हरिपुंगवः
गुणाभिरामं रामं च पुनश्चिन्तापरोऽभवत्

praśasya tu praśastavyāṁ sītāṁ tāṁ haripuṁgavaḥ
guṇābhirāmaṁ rāmaṁ ca punaścintāparo'bhavat
Having eulogized Sita, worthy of being praised and Rama, endeared by accomplishments that foremost of monkeys again engaged in meditation.

स मुहूर्तमिव ध्यात्वा बाष्पपर्याकुलेक्षणः
सीतामाश्रित्य तेजस्वी हनुमान्विललाप ह

sa muhūrtamiva dhyātvā bāṣpaparyākulekṣaṇaḥ
sītāmāśritya tejasvī hanumānvilalāpa ha
Having reflected for some time, the powerful Hanuman, having his eyes full of tears bewailed on Siita's account (in the following strain).

मान्या गुरुविनीतस्य लक्ष्मणस्य गुरुप्रिया
यदि सीतापि दुःखार्ता कालो हि दुरतिक्रमः

mānyā guruvinītasya lakṣmaṇasya gurupriyā
yadi sītāpi duḥkhārtā kālo hi duratikramaḥ
No one can withstand the course of destiny since Sita, being the spouse of the worshipful brother of Laksmana, ever obedient to his elders, has been overwhelmed with grief.

रामस्य व्यवसायज्ञा लक्ष्मणस्य च धीमतः
नात्यर्थं क्षुभ्यते देवी गङ्गेव जलदागमे

rāmasya vyavasāyajñā lakṣmaṇasya ca dhīmataḥ
nātyarthaṁ kṣubhyate devī gaṅgeva jaladāgame
The worshipful damsel is cognizant of the prowess of Rama and the intelligent Laksmana and for this she is not entirely depressed like to the river Ganges at the approach of the rainy season,

तुल्यशीलवयोवृत्तां तुल्याभिजनलक्षणाम्
राघवोऽर्हति वैदेहीं तं चेयमसितेक्षणा

tulyaśīlavayovṛttāṁ tulyābhijanalakṣaṇām
rāghavo'rhati vaidehīṁ taṁ ceyamasitekṣaṇā
As regards their character, age, conduct, family and other auspicious marks they are equal and hence Raghava deserve Vaidehi and this one of dark-blue eyes is his.

तां दृष्ट्वा नवहेमाभां लोककान्तामिव श्रियम्
जगाम मनसा रामं वचनं चेदमब्रवीत्

tāṁ dṛṣṭvā navahemābhāṁ lokakāntāmiva śriyam
jagāma manasā rāmaṁ vacanaṁ cedamabravīt
And having scen seen her, gold-hued and conducing to the happiness of the people like to the Goddess of wealth, Hanuman approached Rama in his mind and said.

अस्या हेतोर्विशालाक्ष्या हतो वाली महाबलः
रावणप्रतिमो वीर्ये कबन्धश्च निपातितः

asyā hetorviśālākṣyā hato vālī mahābalaḥ
rāvaṇapratimo vīrye kabandhaśca nipātitaḥ
For this (damsel) was killed the mighty Vali and Kabandha-Ravana's equal in prowess.

विराधश्च हतः संख्ये राक्षसो भीमविक्रमः
वने रामेण विक्रम्य महेन्द्रेणेव शम्बरः

virādhaśca hataḥ saṁkhye rākṣaso bhīmavikramaḥ
vane rāmeṇa vikramya mahendreṇeva śambaraḥ
For her (too) was destroyed in battle, the terribly powerful Raksasa-Viradha, by Rama putting forth his energy, like to sambara killed by Mahendra.

खरश्च निहतः संख्ये त्रिशिराश्च निपातितः
दूषणश्च महातेजा रामेण विदितात्मना

kharaśca nihataḥ saṁkhye triśirāśca nipātitaḥ
dūṣaṇaśca mahātejā rāmeṇa viditātmanā

(It was for her) that fourteen thousand Raksasas of terrible deeds were destroyed at Janasthana with arrow resembling the flame of fire. And Khara was killed in battle, and Trisira was discomfited and the mighty Dusana by Rama, knowing his ownself.

ऐश्वर्यं वानराणां च दुर्लभं वालिपालितम्
अस्या निमित्ते सुग्रीवः प्राप्तवाँल्लोकसत्कृतम्

aiśvaryaṁ vānarāṇāṁ ca durlabhaṁ vālipālitam
asyā nimitte sugrīvaḥ prāptavā̐llokasatkṛtam
And it was on her account that Sugriva, known all over the world, came by the wealth of the monkeys hard to acquire and amassed by Vali.

सागरश्च मया क्रान्तः श्रीमान्नदनदीपतिः
अस्या हेतोर्विशालाक्ष्याः पुरी चेयं निरीक्षिता

sāgaraśca mayā krāntaḥ śrīmānnadanadīpatiḥ
asyā hetorviśālākṣyāḥ purī ceyaṁ nirīkṣitā
And it is for this (damsel) of expansive eyes that I have crossed the effulgent lord of rivers and have seen this city.

यदि रामः समुद्रान्तां मेदिनीं परिवर्तयेत्
अस्याः कृते जगच्चापि युक्तमित्येव मे मतिः

yadi rāmaḥ samudrāntāṁ medinīṁ parivartayet
asyāḥ kṛte jagaccāpi yuktamityeva me matiḥ
And methinks it would have been all proper had Rama turned on her account the whole earth bounded by oceans.

राज्यं वा त्रिषु लोकेषु सीता वा जनकात्मजा
त्रैलोक्यराज्यं सकलं सीताया नाप्नुयात्कलाम्

rājyaṁ vā triṣu lokeṣu sītā vā janakātmajā
trailokyarājyaṁ sakalaṁ sītāyā nāpnuyātkalām
If the kingdom over the three worlds and the daughter of Janaka be compared together, the former is not equal to one hundredth part of Sita.

उत्थिता मेदिनीं भित्त्वा क्षेत्रे हलमुखक्षते
पद्मरेणुनिभैः कीर्णा शुभैः केदारपांसुभिः

utthitā medinīṁ bhittvā kṣetre halamukhakṣate
padmareṇunibhaiḥ kīrṇā śubhaiḥ kedārapāṁsubhiḥ
This Sita, the daughter of the high-souled Janaka, the pious King of Mithila, firmly attached to her husband, rose, covered with dust, out of the earth, in a field delved by a furrow.

विक्रान्तस्यार्यशीलस्य संयुगेष्वनिवर्तिनः
स्नुषा दशरथस्यैषा ज्येष्ठा राज्ञो यशस्विनी

vikrāntasyāryaśīlasya saṁyugeṣvanivartinaḥ
snuṣā daśarathasyaiṣā jyeṣṭhā rājño yaśasvinī
She is the well-known eldest daughter-in-law of the king Dasaratha, of an adorable character and unchecked prowess.

धर्मज्ञस्य कृतज्ञस्य रामस्य विदितात्मनः
इयं सा दयिता भार्या राक्षसी वशमागता

dharmajñasya kṛtajñasya rāmasya viditātmanaḥ
iyaṁ sā dayitā bhāryā rākṣasī vaśamāgatā
And She is the beloved spouse of the pious and grateful Rama, knowing his ownself, and has been brought under the control of the Raksasis.

सर्वान्भोगान्परित्यज्य भर्तृस्नेहबलात्कृता
अचिन्तयित्वा दुःखानि प्रविष्टा निर्जनं वनम्

sarvānbhogānparityajya bhartṛsnehabalātkṛtā
acintayitvā duḥkhāni praviṣṭā nirjanaṁ vanam
Renouncing all luxuries, and considering not the least about miseries, she actuated by her husband's love entered the solitary forest.

संतुष्टा फलमूलेन भर्तृशुश्रूषणे रता
या परां भजते प्रीतिं वनेऽपि भवने यथा

saṁtuṣṭā phalamūlena bhartṛśuśrūṣaṇe ratā
yā parāṁ bhajate prītiṁ vane'pi bhavane yathā
And satisfied with fruits and roots and ever engaged in her husband's service, she lived in the forest as much delighted as she was in her house.

सेयं कनकवर्णाङ्गी नित्यं सुस्मितभाषिणी
सहते यातनामेतामनर्थानामभागिनी

seyaṁ kanakavarṇāṅgī nityaṁ susmitabhāṣiṇī
sahate yātanāmetāmanarthānāmabhāginī
And that one of a golden hue, never used to afflictions and who was wont to converse always with a delighted countenance, has now been suffering incomparable miseries.

इमां तु शीलसंपन्नां द्रष्टुमिच्छति राघवः
रावणेन प्रमथितां प्रपामिव पिपासितः

imāṁ tu śīlasaṁpannāṁ draṣṭumicchati rāghavaḥ
rāvaṇena pramathitāṁ prapāmiva pipāsitaḥ
Like to a thirsty wight longing for an abode where he might get a drink, Raghava pants after seeing her, gifted with an exalted character and oppressed by Ravana.

अस्या नूनं पुनर्लाभाद्राघवः प्रीतिमेष्यति
राजा राज्यपरिभ्रष्टः पुनः प्राप्येव मेदिनीम्

asyā nūnaṁ punarlābhādrāghavaḥ prītimeṣyati
rājā rājyaparibhraṣṭaḥ punaḥ prāpyeva medinīm
As a monarch who had lost his kingdom, is greatly delighted when he regain it, forsooth shall Raghava, in like manner, be pleased when he shall come by her.

कामभोगैः परित्यक्ता हीना बन्धुजनेन च
धारयत्यात्मनो देहं तत्समागमकाङ्क्षिणी

kāmabhogaiḥ parityaktā hīnā bandhujanena ca
dhārayatyātmano dehaṁ tatsamāgamakāṅkṣiṇī
She too has been maintaining her being in the hope of seeing Rama again, separated as she is from her friends and deprived of all comforts and luxuries.

नैषा पश्यति राक्षस्यो नेमान्पुष्पफलद्रुमान्
एकस्थहृदया नूनं राममेवानुपश्यति

naiṣā paśyati rākṣasyo nemānpuṣpaphaladrumān
ekasthahṛdayā nūnaṁ rāmamevānupaśyati
These Raksasis, and these trees enveloped with fruits and flowers-forsooth she dose not behold, but is engaged with all her heart in medidations only touching Rama.

भर्ता नाम परं नार्या भूषणं भूषणादपि
एषा हि रहिता तेन शोभनार्हा न शोभते

bhartā nāma paraṁ nāryā bhūṣaṇaṁ bhūṣaṇādapi
eṣā hi rahitā tena śobhanārhā na śobhate
Husband enhance the beauty of a female more than the dress (and therefore Sita) beautiful as she is, dose not appear graceful, in her husband's absence.

दुष्करं कुरुते रामो हीनो यदनया प्रभुः
धारयत्यात्मनो देहं न दुःखेनावसीदति

duṣkaraṁ kurute rāmo hīno yadanayā prabhuḥ
dhārayatyātmano dehaṁ na duḥkhenāvasīdati
Forsooth my master Rama has performed a difficult act for he has been still keeping up his life in her separation without consuming himself in grief.

इमामसितकेशान्तां शतपत्रनिभेक्षणाम्
सुखार्हां दुःखितां दृष्ट्वा ममापि व्यथितं मनः

imāmasitakeśāntāṁ śatapatranibhekṣaṇām
sukhārhāṁ duḥkhitāṁ dṛṣṭvā mamāpi vyathitaṁ manaḥ
My heart is greatly pained knowing that she, having dark-blue eyes, resembling lotus petals, worthy of happiness, has been possessed by grief.

क्षितिक्षमा पुष्करसंनिभाक्षी; या रक्षिता राघवलक्ष्मणाभ्याम्
सा राक्षसीभिर्विकृतेक्षणाभिः; संरक्ष्यते संप्रति वृक्षमूले

kṣitikṣamā puṣkarasaṁnibhākṣī; yā rakṣitā rāghavalakṣmaṇābhyām
sā rākṣasībhirvikṛtekṣaṇābhiḥ; saṁrakṣyate saṁprati vṛkṣamūle
She, patient as the Earth, having eyes resembling lotuses, who was ere this protected by Raghava and Laksmana, is now being guarded by Raksasis having terrible eyes, under the trees.

हिमहतनलिनीव नष्टशोभा; व्यसनपरम्परया निपीड्यमाना
सहचररहितेव चक्रवाकी; जनकसुता कृपणां दशां प्रपन्ना

himahatanalinīva naṣṭaśobhā; vyasanaparamparayā nipīḍyamānā
sahacararahiteva cakravākī; janakasutā kṛpaṇāṁ daśāṁ prapannā

Being harassed with continued miseries, the daughter of Janaka has lost all her beauty like to a water-lily crushed with frost, and has come by a miserable plight like to a doe separated from her mate.

अस्या हि पुष्पावनताग्रशाखाः; शोकं दृढं वै जनयत्यशोकाः
हिमव्यपायेन च मन्दरश्मि;रभ्युत्थितो नैकसहस्ररश्मिः

asyā hi puṣpāvanatāgraśākhāḥ; śokaṁ dṛḍhaṁ vai janayatyaśokāḥ
himavyapāyena ca mandaraśmi;rabhyutthito naikasahasraraśmiḥ
The branches of the Asoka trees, lowered down with flowers are as if enhancing her grief as also the Moon of many thousand rays, at the expire of the winter."

इत्येवमर्थं कपिरन्ववेक्ष्य; सीतेयमित्येव निविष्टबुद्धिः
संश्रित्य तस्मिन्निषसाद वृक्षे; बली हरीणामृषभस्तरस्वी

ityevamarthaṁ kapiranvavekṣya; sīteyamityeva niviṣṭabuddhiḥ
saṁśritya tasminniṣasāda vṛkṣe; balī harīṇāmṛṣabhastarasvī
Having reflected thus and arrived at ine conclusion that she was Sita, that powerful leader of monkeys gifted with velocity stationed himself on that tree.

ततः कुमुदषण्डाभो निर्मलं निर्मलः स्वयम्
प्रजगाम नभश्चन्द्रो हंसो नीलमिवोदकम्

tataḥ kumudaṣaṇḍābho nirmalaṁ nirmalaḥ svayam
prajagāma nabhaścandro haṁso nīlamivodakam
Thereupon the Moon, white as water-lily and of clear appearance proceeded far down the welkin like to a goose traversing the blue waters.

साचिव्यमिव कुर्वन्स प्रभया निर्मलप्रभः
चन्द्रमा रश्मिभिः शीतैः सिषेवे पवनात्मजम्

sācivyamiva kurvansa prabhayā nirmalaprabhaḥ
candramā raśmibhiḥ śītaiḥ siṣeve pavanātmajam
With a view to befriend him, the Moon of clear rays, sprinkled the Wind-God's son, with cool beams.

स ददर्श ततः सीतां पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम्
शोकभारैरिव न्यस्तां भारैर्नावमिवाम्भसि

sa dadarśa tataḥ sītāṁ pūrṇacandranibhānanām
śokabhārairiva nyastāṁ bhārairnāvamivāmbhasi
And thereupon he beheld Sita, having a moon-like countenance, plunged in grief like to a laden boat sunk in water.

दिदृक्षमाणो वैदेहीं हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः
स ददर्शाविदूरस्था राक्षसीर्घोरदर्शनाः

didṛkṣamāṇo vaidehīṁ hanūmānmārutātmajaḥ
sa dadarśāvidūrasthā rākṣasīrghoradarśanāḥ
While beholding Vaidehi, Hanuman, the son of Maruta, observed at some distance, a number of grim-visaged Raksasis.

एकाक्षीमेककर्णां च कर्णप्रावरणां तथा
अकर्णां शङ्कुकर्णां च मस्तकोच्छ्वासनासिकाम्

ekākṣīmekakarṇāṁ ca karṇaprāvaraṇāṁ tathā
akarṇāṁ śaṅkukarṇāṁ ca mastakocchvāsanāsikām
Some had one ear, some one eye, some had big ears some was without ears; some had formidable ears and some had a nose projecting upwards.

अतिकायोत्तमाङ्गीं च तनुदीर्घशिरोधराम्
ध्वस्तकेशीं तथाकेशीं केशकम्बलधारिणीम्

atikāyottamāṅgīṁ ca tanudīrghaśirodharām
dhvastakeśīṁ tathākeśīṁ keśakambaladhāriṇīm

And some had the upper part of their bodies unusually long and bulky, some had a long and slender neck, some had dishevelled hair, and some one's person was so thickly covered with hairs, that she appeared to have been cloaked in a blanket.

लम्बकर्णललाटां च लम्बोदरपयोधराम्
लम्बौष्ठीं चिबुकौष्ठीं च लम्बास्यां लम्बजानुकाम्

lambakarṇalalāṭāṁ ca lambodarapayodharām
lambauṣṭhīṁ cibukauṣṭhīṁ ca lambāsyāṁ lambajānukām

Some had long ears some had a long forehead, some had a long belly, some had long breasts; some had long lips; some had their lips and chins stuck together, some had a long countenance and some had long knees.

ह्रस्वां दीर्घां च कुब्जां च विकटां वामनां तथा
करालां भुग्नवस्त्रां च पिङ्गाक्षीं विकृताननाम्

hrasvāṁ dīrghāṁ ca kubjāṁ ca vikaṭāṁ vāmanāṁ tathā
karālāṁ bhugnavastrāṁ ca piṅgākṣīṁ vikṛtānanām

Some one was of-short stature, some was tall, some crooked, some grim-visaged, some dwarfish, some one was of terribly dark colour; some had a disfigured countenance; some had coppery eyes and a fearful face.

विकृताः पिङ्गलाः कालीः क्रोधनाः कलहप्रियाः
कालायसमहाशूलकूटमुद्गरधारिणीः

vikṛtāḥ piṅgalāḥ kālīḥ krodhanāḥ kalahapriyāḥ
kālāyasamahāśūlakūṭamudgaradhāriṇīḥ
Some were terrible-looking, some coppercoloured, some black, some angry and some fond of quarrelling with each other; and some had iron darts, hammers and mallets in their hands.

वराहमृगशार्दूलमहिषाजशिवा मुखाः
गजोष्ट्रहयपादाश्च निखातशिरसोऽपराः

varāhamṛgaśārdūlamahiṣājaśivā mukhāḥ
gajoṣṭrahayapādāśca nikhātaśiraso'parāḥ

Some had a face like that of a boar, some had a face like that of a deer, some like that of a tiger, some like that of a buffalo, some like that of a goat, and some like that of a jackal; some had legs like those of a camel, some had those of an elephant, some those of a horse and some had their heads placed on their breasts.

एकहस्तैकपादाश्च खरकर्ण्यश्वकर्णिकाः
गोकर्णीर्हस्तिकर्णीश्च हरिकर्णीस्तथापराः

ekahastaikapādāśca kharakarṇyaśvakarṇikāḥ
gokarṇīrhastikarṇīśca harikarṇīstathāparāḥ

Some one had only one hand some had only one leg. Some had ears like those of a horse, some like those of a cow, some like those of an ass, some like those of an elephant and others had ears like those of a lion.

अनासा अतिनासाश्च तिर्यन्नासा विनासिकाः
गजसंनिभनासाश्च ललाटोच्छ्वासनासिकाः

anāsā atināsāśca tiryannāsā vināsikāḥ
gajasaṁnibhanāsāśca lalāṭocchvāsanāsikāḥ
Some had very big noses, some had crooked and others were without any; some had noses like those of an elephant and others had their noses on their foreheads.

हस्तिपादा महापादा गोपादाः पादचूलिकाः
अतिमात्रशिरोग्रीवा अतिमात्रकुचोदरीः

hastipādā mahāpādā gopādāḥ pādacūlikāḥ
atimātraśirogrīvā atimātrakucodarīḥ

Some had their legs like those of elephants some had very huge legs; some and like those of a cow, some had on their legs locks of hair like to pillars, some had a terribly huge head, some had big breasts and others had spacious bellies, Some had faces and eyes beyond ordinary proportions.

अतिमात्रास्य नेत्राश्च दीर्घजिह्वानखास्तथा
अजामुखीर्हस्तिमुखीर्गोमुखीः सूकरीमुखीः

atimātrāsya netrāśca dīrghajihvānakhāstathā
ajāmukhīrhastimukhīrgomukhīḥ sūkarīmukhīḥ
Some had a long face and tongue. And some had the face of a goat, some that of an elephant some that of a cow, some that of a boar some that of a horse and some that of an ass.

मांसशोणितदिग्धाङ्गीर्मांसशोणितभोजनाः
ता ददर्श कपिश्रेष्ठो रोमहर्षणदर्शनाः

māṁsaśoṇitadigdhāṅgīrmāṁsaśoṇitabhojanāḥ
tā dadarśa kapiśreṣṭho romaharṣaṇadarśanāḥ

Some of the Raksasis were grim-visaged and some hot-natured, quarrelsome and had darts andmaces in their hands. And some terrible Raks asis of disfigured countenances, had smokycoloured hairs. And they were all continually drinking wine, always fond of liquor and meat, and all their bodies were sprinkled with blood for their living on gore and flesh.

स्कन्धवन्तमुपासीनाः परिवार्य वनस्पतिम्
तस्याधस्ताच्च तां देवीं राजपुत्रीमनिन्दिताम्

skandhavantamupāsīnāḥ parivārya vanaspatim
tasyādhastācca tāṁ devīṁ rājaputrīmaninditām

And that foremost of monkeys found all these grim-visaged Raksasis seated around that mighty tree enveloped with branches. And the graceful Hanuman observed at the foot of that tree that worshipful and blameless daughter of the king Janaka. She was bereft of all effulgence, racked with grief and all her hairs were soiled with dirt. no

क्षीणपुण्यां च्युतां भूमौ तारां निपतितामिव
चारित्र्य व्यपदेशाढ्यां भर्तृदर्शनदुर्गताम्

kṣīṇapuṇyāṁ cyutāṁ bhūmau tārāṁ nipatitāmiva
cāritrya vyapadeśāḍhyāṁ bhartṛdarśanadurgatām
She appeared like a star fallen down on the earth on the wane of virtue. And famed though she was all over the world for her chastity, it was difficult for her now to see her husband.

भूषणैरुत्तमैर्हीनां भर्तृवात्सल्यभूषिताम्
राक्षसाधिपसंरुद्धां बन्धुभिश्च विनाकृताम्

bhūṣaṇairuttamairhīnāṁ bhartṛvātsalyabhūṣitām
rākṣasādhipasaṁruddhāṁ bandhubhiśca vinākṛtām

She had excellent ornaments-her attachment to her husband was the only ornament. She was imprisoned by the lord of Raksasas and separated from all her friends, she appeared like a she elephant separated from her band and bound and attacked by a lion, and like the rays of the Moon enveloped with clouds at the expire of the rainy season,

क्लिष्टरूपामसंस्पर्शादयुक्तामिव वल्लकीम्
सीतां भर्तृहिते युक्तामयुक्तां रक्षसां वशे

kliṣṭarūpāmasaṁsparśādayuktāmiva vallakīm
sītāṁ bhartṛhite yuktāmayuktāṁ rakṣasāṁ vaśe

Her beauty was greatly faded (in consequence of her husband's separation) like to a stringed instrument for want of a player. And ever engaged in her husband's welfare she was thoroughly unworthy of being brought under the control of the Raksasas. Being sunk in the abyss of grief and encircled by those Raksasis she appeared in the forest of Asoka like to Rohini possessed by Rahu.

सा मलेन च दिग्धाङ्गी वपुषा चाप्यलंकृता
मृणाली पङ्कदिग्धेव विभाति च न भाति च

sā malena ca digdhāṅgī vapuṣā cāpyalaṁkṛtā
mṛṇālī paṅkadigdheva vibhāti ca na bhāti ca
And Hanuman beheld her there like a creeper divested of flowers. And having her person soiled with dirt and shorn of all ornaments she appeared in her hidden grace like to a lotus covered with clay.

मलिनेन तु वस्त्रेण परिक्लिष्टेन भामिनीम्
संवृतां मृगशावाक्षीं ददर्श हनुमान्कपिः

malinena tu vastreṇa parikliṣṭena bhāminīm
saṁvṛtāṁ mṛgaśāvākṣīṁ dadarśa hanumānkapiḥ
The monkey Hanuman, beheld that damsel, having the eyes of a young antelope, clothed with a soiled and shattered cloth.

तां देवीं दीनवदनामदीनां भर्तृतेजसा
रक्षितां स्वेन शीलेन सीतामसितलोचनाम्

tāṁ devīṁ dīnavadanāmadīnāṁ bhartṛtejasā
rakṣitāṁ svena śīlena sītāmasitalocanām
And though the countenance of that worshipful one was shorn of all grace, her heart did not loose its loftiness in consequence of her husband's prowess.

प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे मारुतिः प्रेक्ष्य मैथिलीम्
हर्षजानि च सोऽश्रूणि तां दृष्ट्वा मदिरेक्षणाम्
मुमोच हनुमांस्तत्र नमश्चक्रे च राघवम्

praharṣamatulaṁ lebhe mārutiḥ prekṣya maithilīm
harṣajāni ca so'śrūṇi tāṁ dṛṣṭvā madirekṣaṇām
mumoca hanumāṁstatra namaścakre ca rāghavam
And beholding her having inebriate eyes, Hanuman shed tears of delight and bowed to Raghava.

नमस्कृत्वा च रामाय लक्ष्मणाय च वीर्यवान्
सीतादर्शनसंहृष्टो हनूमान्संवृतोऽभवत्

namaskṛtvā ca rāmāya lakṣmaṇāya ca vīryavān
sītādarśanasaṁhṛṣṭo hanūmānsaṁvṛto'bhavat
Having offered his obeisance to Rama and Laksmana the powerful Hanuman, greatly delighted in seeing Sita, remained there hidden.

तथा विप्रेक्षमाणस्य वनं पुष्पितपादपम्
विचिन्वतश्च वैदेहीं किंचिच्छेषा निशाभवत्

tathā viprekṣamāṇasya vanaṁ puṣpitapādapam
vicinvataśca vaidehīṁ kiṁciccheṣā niśābhavat
Beholding the forest filled with flowery trees and desiring to have a full view of her, he, wellnigh, spent the night.

षडङ्गवेदविदुषां क्रतुप्रवरयाजिनाम्
शुश्राव ब्रह्मघोषांश्च विरात्रे ब्रह्मरक्षसाम्

ṣaḍaṅgavedaviduṣāṁ kratupravarayājinām
śuśrāva brahmaghoṣāṁśca virātre brahmarakṣasām

At that late hour of the night, he heard the chantings of the Vedas by the Raksasas, conversant with the six supplementary parts of the Vedas,* engaged in the performance of sacrificial rites and knowing Brahma. *Grammar, Prosody, astronomy, pronounciation, the meaning of the unusual terms and the ritual of the Hindu religion.

अथ मङ्गलवादित्रैः शब्दैः श्रोत्रमनोहरैः
प्राबोध्यत महाबाहुर्दशग्रीवो महाबलः

atha maṅgalavāditraiḥ śabdaiḥ śrotramanoharaiḥ
prābodhyata mahābāhurdaśagrīvo mahābalaḥ
And thereupon the mighty Ten-headed Raksasa, having huge arms, awoke with the sounds of those auspicious instruments, pleasant to ears.

विबुध्य तु यथाकालं राक्षसेन्द्रः प्रतावपान्
स्रस्तमाल्याम्बरधरो वैदेहीमन्वचिन्तयत्

vibudhya tu yathākālaṁ rākṣasendraḥ pratāvapān
srastamālyāmbaradharo vaidehīmanvacintayat
Awaking, that great and powerful lord of Raksasas, having his cloth and garlands loosened, began to think of Vaidehi.

भृशं नियुक्तस्तस्यां च मदनेन मदोत्कटः
न स तं राक्षसः कामं शशाकात्मनि गूहितुम्

bhṛśaṁ niyuktastasyāṁ ca madanena madotkaṭaḥ
na sa taṁ rākṣasaḥ kāmaṁ śaśākātmani gūhitum
That Raksasa, puffed up with pride, was passionately attached to her and so he could not restrain his amour in him.

अङ्गनाशतमात्रं तु तं व्रजन्तमनुव्रजत्
महेन्द्रमिव पौलस्त्यं देवगन्धर्वयोषितः

aṅganāśatamātraṁ tu taṁ vrajantamanuvrajat
mahendramiva paulastyaṁ devagandharvayoṣitaḥ
And one hundred damsels followed in the train of the son of Pulastya like to the damsels of the celestials and Gandharvas following mahendra. 'Refers to Ravana, Pulastya being his father.

दीपिकाः काञ्चनीः काश्चिज्जगृहुस्तत्र योषितः
बालव्यजनहस्ताश्च तालवृन्तानि चापराः

dīpikāḥ kāñcanīḥ kāścijjagṛhustatra yoṣitaḥ
bālavyajanahastāśca tālavṛntāni cāparāḥ
There among those fair ones, some carried torches with gold handles, chowries and some fans.

काञ्चनैरपि भृङ्गारैर्जह्रुः सलिलमग्रतः
मण्डलाग्रानसींश्चैव गृह्यान्याः पृष्ठतो ययुः

kāñcanairapi bhṛṅgārairjahruḥ salilamagrataḥ
maṇḍalāgrānasīṁścaiva gṛhyānyāḥ pṛṣṭhato yayuḥ
Some carrying water in golden jars headed the train while others carrying the golden throne covered with a coverlet followed it.

काचिद्रत्नमयीं पात्रीं पूर्णां पानस्य भामिनी
दक्षिणा दक्षिणेनैव तदा जग्राह पाणिना

kācidratnamayīṁ pātrīṁ pūrṇāṁ pānasya bhāminī
dakṣiṇā dakṣiṇenaiva tadā jagrāha pāṇinā
And a favourite damsel carried in her right hand a jewelled drinking bowl filled with wine.

राजहंसप्रतीकाशं छत्रं पूर्णशशिप्रभम्
सौवर्णदण्डमपरा गृहीत्वा पृष्ठतो ययौ

rājahaṁsapratīkāśaṁ chatraṁ pūrṇaśaśiprabham
sauvarṇadaṇḍamaparā gṛhītvā pṛṣṭhato yayau
Another carrying the white umbrella having golden ribs resembling the full moon and goose, followed in the train.

निद्रामदपरीताक्ष्यो रावणस्योत्तमस्त्रियः
अनुजग्मुः पतिं वीरं घनं विद्युल्लता इव

nidrāmadaparītākṣyo rāvaṇasyottamastriyaḥ
anujagmuḥ patiṁ vīraṁ ghanaṁ vidyullatā iva
And in this wise the excellent wives, of Ravana, having their eyes rendered sleepy with sleep and wine, followed their heroic husband like to lightings following the cloud.

ततः काञ्चीनिनादं च नूपुराणां च निःस्वनम्
शुश्राव परमस्त्रीणां स कपिर्मारुतात्मजः

tataḥ kāñcīninādaṁ ca nūpurāṇāṁ ca niḥsvanam
śuśrāva paramastrīṇāṁ sa kapirmārutātmajaḥ
And that monkey, son of Maruta, heard the sound of kancis and nupuras of those excellent damsels.

तं चाप्रतिमकर्माणमचिन्त्यबलपौरुषम्
द्वारदेशमनुप्राप्तं ददर्श हनुमान्कपिः

taṁ cāpratimakarmāṇamacintyabalapauruṣam
dvāradeśamanuprāptaṁ dadarśa hanumānkapiḥ
And the monkey Hanuman also beheld Ravana, of extraordinary deeds and of inconceivable prowess and strength, at the gate.

दीपिकाभिरनेकाभिः समन्तादवभासितम्
गन्धतैलावसिक्ताभिर्ध्रियमाणाभिरग्रतः

dīpikābhiranekābhiḥ samantādavabhāsitam
gandhatailāvasiktābhirdhriyamāṇābhiragrataḥ
His whole body was seen on all sides by the light of the lamps lighted with perfumed oil and carried by the Raksasis before.

कामदर्पमदैर्युक्तं जिह्मताम्रायतेक्षणम्
समक्षमिव कन्दर्पमपविद्ध शरासनम्

kāmadarpamadairyuktaṁ jihmatāmrāyatekṣaṇam
samakṣamiva kandarpamapaviddha śarāsanam
He was inflamed with amour, pride and haughtiness and his expansive eyes were coppery and idle. And he appeared like Cupid himself just appearing in view, leaving behind his bow and arrows.

मथितामृतफेनाभमरजो वस्त्रमुत्तमम्
सलीलमनुकर्षन्तं विमुक्तं सक्तमङ्गदे

mathitāmṛtaphenābhamarajo vastramuttamam
salīlamanukarṣantaṁ vimuktaṁ saktamaṅgade
Holding his excellent robe, covered with flowers, washed, set with jewels and white as the foam of the churned nectar, he placed it in its proper place.

तं पत्रविटपे लीनः पत्रपुष्पघनावृतः
समीपमुपसंक्रान्तं निध्यातुमुपचक्रमे

taṁ patraviṭape līnaḥ patrapuṣpaghanāvṛtaḥ
samīpamupasaṁkrāntaṁ nidhyātumupacakrame
Hanuman, hiding himself on the tree, in the midst of many leaves and flowers, tried to recognise him as he approached.

ताभिः परिवृतो राजा सुरूपाभिर्महायशाः
तन्मृगद्विजसंघुष्टं प्रविष्टः प्रमदावनम्

tābhiḥ parivṛto rājā surūpābhirmahāyaśāḥ
tanmṛgadvijasaṁghuṣṭaṁ praviṣṭaḥ pramadāvanam
Beholding him, that foremost of monkeys saw that highly famous king Ravana, surrounded by his excellently beautiful and youthful wives, enter that forest of enjoyment filled with birds and animals.

क्षीबो विचित्राभरणः शङ्कुकर्णो महाबलः
तेन विश्रवसः पुत्रः स दृष्टो राक्षसाधिपः

kṣībo vicitrābharaṇaḥ śaṅkukarṇo mahābalaḥ
tena viśravasaḥ putraḥ sa dṛṣṭo rākṣasādhipaḥ
There was a warder by name Sankukarna in that forest—highly powerful, wearing various ornaments and addicted to drinking. And by him was seen that lord of Raksasas—the son of Visrava.

रावणोऽयं महाबाहुरिति संचिन्त्य वानरः
अवप्लुतो महातेजा हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः

rāvaṇo'yaṁ mahābāhuriti saṁcintya vānaraḥ
avapluto mahātejā hanūmānmārutātmajaḥ

That highly energetic monkey beheld that effulgent (Ravana) surrounded by excellent damsels like to moon encircled by stars. And beholding him the monkey reflected—“This must be Ravana-for he is the person whom I saw sleeping in an excellent apartment in that city.” Thinking this, that highly effulgent son of Maruta-Hanuman leaped (high upon another branch).

स तथाप्युग्रतेजाः सन्निर्धूतस्तस्य तेजसा
पत्रगुह्यान्तरे सक्तो हनूमान्संवृतोऽभवत्

sa tathāpyugratejāḥ sannirdhūtastasya tejasā
patraguhyāntare sakto hanūmānsaṁvṛto'bhavat
And effulgent as he was, that highly intelligent monkey hid himself on a branch covered with leaves, being unable to stand before the effulgence of that Raksasa.

स तामसितकेशान्तां सुश्रोणीं संहतस्तनीम्
दिदृक्षुरसितापाङ्गीमुपावर्तत रावणः

sa tāmasitakeśāntāṁ suśroṇīṁ saṁhatastanīm
didṛkṣurasitāpāṅgīmupāvartata rāvaṇaḥ
Ravana proceeded in that way, being anxious to behold the blue-eyed Sita, having spacious breast, excellent hips and a lock of black hair.

तस्मिन्नेव ततः काले राजपुत्री त्वनिन्दिता
रूपयौवनसंपन्नं भूषणोत्तमभूषितम्

tasminneva tataḥ kāle rājaputrī tvaninditā
rūpayauvanasaṁpannaṁ bhūṣaṇottamabhūṣitam

Thereupon beholding Ravana-the lord of Raksasas, gifted with youth and beauty and adorned with an excellent dress, that excellent and blameless daughter of a king, Vaidehi, trembled like to a plantain tree shaken by the wind.

ऊरुभ्यामुदरं छाद्य बाहुभ्यां च पयोधरौ
उपविष्टा विशालाक्षी रुदन्ती वरवर्णिनी

ūrubhyāmudaraṁ chādya bāhubhyāṁ ca payodharau
upaviṣṭā viśālākṣī rudantī varavarṇinī
Having covered her belly with her legs and her breast with her hands, that one, having charming colour and expansive eyes, cried aloud.

दशग्रीवस्तु वैदेहीं रक्षितां राक्षसीगणैः
ददर्श दीनां दुःखार्तं नावं सन्नामिवार्णवे

daśagrīvastu vaidehīṁ rakṣitāṁ rākṣasīgaṇaiḥ
dadarśa dīnāṁ duḥkhārtaṁ nāvaṁ sannāmivārṇave

Arriving there the Ten-necked one beheld Vaidehi, guarded by the Raksasis, poorly, racked with grief like to a boat sunk in an ocean. Subject to hard penances, she, seated on the bare earth, appeared like a branch of a tree fallen on the ground

समीपं राजसिंहस्य रामस्य विदितात्मनः
संकल्पहयसंयुक्तैर्यान्तीमिव मनोरथैः

samīpaṁ rājasiṁhasya rāmasya viditātmanaḥ
saṁkalpahayasaṁyuktairyāntīmiva manorathaiḥ
She was proceeding as it were to that lion of a king-Rama, knowing his own-self, in her mind's chariot drawn by the horses of resolution.

शुष्यन्तीं रुदतीमेकां ध्यानशोकपरायणाम्
दुःखस्यान्तमपश्यन्तीं रामां राममनुव्रताम्

śuṣyantīṁ rudatīmekāṁ dhyānaśokaparāyaṇām
duḥkhasyāntamapaśyantīṁ rāmāṁ rāmamanuvratām
And not beholding the end of her grief, that damsel, attached to Rama, was keeping alone and reduced to a skeleton and overwhelmed with anxious thoughts and grief.

वेष्टमानामथाविष्टां पन्नगेन्द्रवधूमिव
धूप्यमानां ग्रहेणेव रोहिणीं धूमकेतुना

veṣṭamānāmathāviṣṭāṁ pannagendravadhūmiva
dhūpyamānāṁ graheṇeva rohiṇīṁ dhūmaketunā
She was troubled like to the daughter-in-law of the lord of serpents, of impeded course by means of incantations, and stricken with grief like to Rohini, possessed by Ketu.

वृत्तशीले कुले जातामाचारवति धार्मिके
पुनः संस्कारमापन्नां जातमिव च दुष्कुले

vṛttaśīle kule jātāmācāravati dhārmike
punaḥ saṁskāramāpannāṁ jātamiva ca duṣkule

And although born in a pious family, well behaved and good-natured and married according to their rites, she appeared to have been sprung form a low race and wedded according to their base ceremonials.

पतिशोकातुरां शुष्कां नदीं विस्रावितामिव
परया मृजया हीनां कृष्णपक्षे निशामिव

patiśokāturāṁ śuṣkāṁ nadīṁ visrāvitāmiva
parayā mṛjayā hīnāṁ kṛṣṇapakṣe niśāmiva
And her grace greatly famished by the absence of her husband she appeared like a river whose liquid contents were dried up. And not cleaning her limbs she appeared like a dark night.

सुकुमारीं सुजाताङ्गीं रत्नगर्भगृहोचिताम्
तप्यमानामिवोष्णेन मृणालीमचिरोद्धृताम्

sukumārīṁ sujātāṅgīṁ ratnagarbhagṛhocitām
tapyamānāmivoṣṇena mṛṇālīmaciroddhṛtām
That one of graceful limbs, tender and worthy of living in a jewelled abode, being stricken with grief, seemed like a dried lotus-stalk just extracted from its bed.

गृहीतामालितां स्तम्भे यूथपेन विनाकृताम्
निःश्वसन्तीं सुदुःखार्तां गजराजवधूमिव

gṛhītāmālitāṁ stambhe yūthapena vinākṛtām
niḥśvasantīṁ suduḥkhārtāṁ gajarājavadhūmiva
And she like the daughter-in-law of the lord of elephants, caught, separated from her band and tied to a pillar, was overwhelmed with grief and was sighing again and again.

एकया दीर्घया वेण्या शोभमानामयत्नतः
नीलया नीरदापाये वनराज्या महीमिव

ekayā dīrghayā veṇyā śobhamānāmayatnataḥ
nīlayā nīradāpāye vanarājyā mahīmiva
A long lock of dark-blue hair, taken not the least care of, was on her back; and with this she appeared like to the earth covered with dark-blue forests at the expiration of the rainy season.

उपवासेन शोकेन ध्यानेन च भयेन च
परिक्षीणां कृशां दीनामल्पाहारां तपोधनाम्

upavāsena śokena dhyānena ca bhayena ca
parikṣīṇāṁ kṛśāṁ dīnāmalpāhārāṁ tapodhanām
With fasts and grief, anxiety and fear, she was greatly weakened and reduced and gave up cating and took recourse to asceticism only.

आयाचमानां दुःखार्तां प्राञ्जलिं देवतामिव
भावेन रघुमुख्यस्य दशग्रीवपराभवम्

āyācamānāṁ duḥkhārtāṁ prāñjaliṁ devatāmiva
bhāvena raghumukhyasya daśagrīvaparābhavam
Stricken with grief, she seemed to have been offering prayers to that foremost of Raghus for the destruction of the Ten-necked one, like those to the deities with folded hands.

समीक्षमाणां रुदतीमनिन्दितां; सुपक्ष्मताम्रायतशुक्ललोचनाम्
अनुव्रतां राममतीव मैथिलीं; प्रलोभयामास वधाय रावणः

samīkṣamāṇāṁ rudatīmaninditāṁ; supakṣmatāmrāyataśuklalocanām
anuvratāṁ rāmamatīva maithilīṁ; pralobhayāmāsa vadhāya rāvaṇaḥ
Beholding that blameless Maithili, having expansive eyes with beautiful eye lashes, greatly attached to Rama, and weeping Ravana tempted her for his own destruction.

स तां परिवृतां दीनां निरानन्दां तपस्विनीम्
साकारैर्मधुरैर्वाक्यैर्न्यदर्शयत रावणः

sa tāṁ parivṛtāṁ dīnāṁ nirānandāṁ tapasvinīm
sākārairmadhurairvākyairnyadarśayata rāvaṇaḥ
Thereupon Ravana, with sweet words and gestures, expressed his own desire to Sita, poorly, deprived of joy, encircled by Raksasis and leading the life of an ascetic.

मां दृष्ट्वा नागनासोरुगूहमाना स्तनोदरम्
अदर्शनमिवात्मानं भयान्नेतुं त्वमिच्छसि

māṁ dṛṣṭvā nāganāsorugūhamānā stanodaram
adarśanamivātmānaṁ bhayānnetuṁ tvamicchasi
O you having thighs like the trunks of elephants, while you had, beholding me, hidden your breast and belly, perhaps you are afraid of exposing your person to me.

कामये त्वां विशालाक्षि बहुमन्यस्व मां प्रिये
सर्वाङ्गगुणसंपन्ने सर्वलोकमनोहरे

kāmaye tvāṁ viśālākṣi bahumanyasva māṁ priye
sarvāṅgaguṇasaṁpanne sarvalokamanohare
I do long for you, O you having expansive eyes; do you esteem me, O my dear one, O you gifted with all accomplishments and pleasant to all persons.

नेह केचिन्मनुष्या वा राक्षसाः कामरूपिणः
व्यपसर्पतु ते सीते भयं मत्तः समुत्थितम्

neha kecinmanuṣyā vā rākṣasāḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ
vyapasarpatu te sīte bhayaṁ mattaḥ samutthitam
O Sita, here is no human being or any Raksasa assuming shapes at will, do you therefore renounce all fear from me.

स्वधर्मे रक्षसां भीरु सर्वथैष न संशयः
गमनं वा परस्त्रीणां हरणं संप्रमथ्य वा

svadharme rakṣasāṁ bhīru sarvathaiṣa na saṁśayaḥ
gamanaṁ vā parastrīṇāṁ haraṇaṁ saṁpramathya vā
O timid damsel, for certain it is the virtue of the Raksasas that they always visit others' wives or come by them by force.

एवं चैतदकामां च न त्वां स्प्रक्ष्यामि मैथिलि
कामं कामः शरीरे मे यथाकामं प्रवर्तताम्

evaṁ caitadakāmāṁ ca na tvāṁ sprakṣyāmi maithili
kāmaṁ kāmaḥ śarīre me yathākāmaṁ pravartatām
In spite of this, O Maithili, I do not touch you for you are not under the influence of amour—but for me, I am completely under its sway.

देवि नेह भयं कार्यं मयि विश्वसिहि प्रिये
प्रणयस्व च तत्त्वेन मैवं भूः शोकलालसा

devi neha bhayaṁ kāryaṁ mayi viśvasihi priye
praṇayasva ca tattvena maivaṁ bhūḥ śokalālasā
Do not fear me, O worshipful damsel, confide in me O my beloved one, and become attached to me. Do not give way to grief.

एकवेणी धराशय्या ध्यानं मलिनमम्बरम्
अस्थानेऽप्युपवासश्च नैतान्यौपयिकानि ते

ekaveṇī dharāśayyā dhyānaṁ malinamambaram
asthāne'pyupavāsaśca naitānyaupayikāni te
A single lock of hair, to lie down on earth and useless fast-these do not become you.

विचित्राणि च माल्यानि चन्दनान्यगरूणि च
विविधानि च वासांसि दिव्यान्याभरणानि च

vicitrāṇi ca mālyāni candanānyagarūṇi ca
vividhāni ca vāsāṁsi divyānyābharaṇāni ca
Attaining me, O Maithili, do you enjoy excellent garlands, sandal, ornaments, costly wines, beds, seats, songs, dancing and music.

स्त्रीरत्नमसि मैवं भूः कुरु गात्रेषु भूषणम्
मां प्राप्य तु कथं हि स्यास्त्वमनर्हा सुविग्रहे

strīratnamasi maivaṁ bhūḥ kuru gātreṣu bhūṣaṇam
māṁ prāpya tu kathaṁ hi syāstvamanarhā suvigrahe
You are a jewel of a female; do you not therefore remain in this guise. Put on your ornaments therefore. How shall you remain unadorned obtaining me, O you of a beautiful figure?

इदं ते चारुसंजातं यौवनं व्यतिवर्तते
यदतीतं पुनर्नैति स्रोतः शीघ्रमपामिव

idaṁ te cārusaṁjātaṁ yauvanaṁ vyativartate
yadatītaṁ punarnaiti srotaḥ śīghramapāmiva
This your beautiful youth is passing away, which like the current of a river when once gone, dose not turn back,

त्वां कृत्वोपरतो मन्ये रूपकर्ता स विश्वकृत्
न हि रूपोपमा त्वन्या तवास्ति शुभदर्शने

tvāṁ kṛtvoparato manye rūpakartā sa viśvakṛt
na hi rūpopamā tvanyā tavāsti śubhadarśane
O you of a fair look, having created you, the artist of Gods, the maker of celestial beauties, has ceased from his work, for a match of your beauty I find in none.

त्वां समासाद्य वैदेहि रूपयौवनशालिनीम्
कः पुमानतिवर्तेत साक्षादपि पितामहः

tvāṁ samāsādya vaidehi rūpayauvanaśālinīm
kaḥ pumānativarteta sākṣādapi pitāmahaḥ
Who is there, O Vaidehi, who can withstand the influence of amour, getting you, gifted with beauty and youth? (What of others) even Brahma, the grand-father of the celestials, is moved.

यद्यत्पश्यामि ते गात्रं शीतांशुसदृशानने
तस्मिंस्तस्मिन्पृथुश्रोणि चक्षुर्मम निबध्यते

yadyatpaśyāmi te gātraṁ śītāṁśusadṛśānane
tasmiṁstasminpṛthuśroṇi cakṣurmama nibadhyate
O you having a moon-like countenance, and well-developed hips, whatever limbs of yours, I behold, I find my gaze fixed therein.

भव मैथिलि भार्या मे मोहमेनं विसर्जय
बह्वीनामुत्तमस्त्रीणां ममाग्रमहिषी भव

bhava maithili bhāryā me mohamenaṁ visarjaya
bahvīnāmuttamastrīṇāṁ mamāgramahiṣī bhava
O Maithili, do you become my spouse, and renounce this delusion. Do you become the foremost queen of all my excellent wives.

लोकेभ्यो यानि रत्नानि संप्रमथ्याहृतानि मे
तानि ते भीरु सर्वाणि राज्यं चैतदहं च ते

lokebhyo yāni ratnāni saṁpramathyāhṛtāni me
tāni te bhīru sarvāṇi rājyaṁ caitadahaṁ ca te
O timid one, all the jewels that I have collected from the three worlds, and all my kingdom I shall confer on you.

विजित्य पृथिवीं सर्वां नानानगरमालिनीम्
जनकाय प्रदास्यामि तव हेतोर्विलासिनि

vijitya pṛthivīṁ sarvāṁ nānānagaramālinīm
janakāya pradāsyāmi tava hetorvilāsini
O sportive damsel, for your satisfaction, I shall conquer the whole earth, engarlanded by many cities and bestow it upon Janaka.

नेह पश्यामि लोकेऽन्यं यो मे प्रतिबलो भवेत्
पश्य मे सुमहद्वीर्यमप्रतिद्वन्द्वमाहवे

neha paśyāmi loke'nyaṁ yo me pratibalo bhavet
paśya me sumahadvīryamapratidvandvamāhave
Find I none on this earth who can withstand my prowess. Do you behold my matchless prowess in battle.

असकृत्संयुगे भग्ना मया विमृदितध्वजाः
अशक्ताः प्रत्यनीकेषु स्थातुं मम सुरासुराः

asakṛtsaṁyuge bhagnā mayā vimṛditadhvajāḥ
aśaktāḥ pratyanīkeṣu sthātuṁ mama surāsurāḥ
The celestials and Asuras are incapable of withstanding me, defeated as they were by me in battle and their pennons struck down.

इच्छ मां क्रियतामद्य प्रतिकर्म तवोत्तमम्
सप्रभाण्यवसज्जन्तां तवाङ्गे भूषणानि च
साधु पश्यामि ते रूपं संयुक्तं प्रतिकर्मणा

iccha māṁ kriyatāmadya pratikarma tavottamam
saprabhāṇyavasajjantāṁ tavāṅge bhūṣaṇāni ca
sādhu paśyāmi te rūpaṁ saṁyuktaṁ pratikarmaṇā
Do you therefore desire ine to-day, dress yourself in excellent robes and adorn yourself in beautifully brilliant ornaments.

प्रतिकर्माभिसंयुक्ता दाक्षिण्येन वरानने
भुङ्क्ष्व भोगान्यथाकामं पिब भीरु रमस्व च
यथेष्टं च प्रयच्छ त्वं पृथिवीं वा धनानि च

pratikarmābhisaṁyuktā dākṣiṇyena varānane
bhuṅkṣva bhogānyathākāmaṁ piba bhīru ramasva ca
yatheṣṭaṁ ca prayaccha tvaṁ pṛthivīṁ vā dhanāni ca
O timid damsel, do you, at your pleasure, enjoy all sorts of comforts and luxuries, and do you, as you desirest, confer wealth and land on others.

ललस्व मयि विस्रब्धा धृष्टमाज्ञापयस्व च
मत्प्रभावाल्ललन्त्याश्च ललन्तां बान्धवास्तव

lalasva mayi visrabdhā dhṛṣṭamājñāpayasva ca
matprabhāvāllalantyāśca lalantāṁ bāndhavāstava
Do you confiding in me, ask for your wishedfor objects and do you command me like to an unmannerly damsel. You shall, by asking favours from me, satisfy the desires of your friends.

ऋद्धिं ममानुपश्य त्वं श्रियं भद्रे यशश्च मे
किं करिष्यसि रामेण सुभगे चीरवाससा

ṛddhiṁ mamānupaśya tvaṁ śriyaṁ bhadre yaśaśca me
kiṁ kariṣyasi rāmeṇa subhage cīravāsasā
Ogently lady, O you of great renown, do you observe my prosperity. What shall you do with Rama, wearing bark, O you of pleasant presence.

निक्षिप्तविजयो रामो गतश्रीर्वनगोचरः
व्रती स्थण्डिलशायी च शङ्के जीवति वा न वा

nikṣiptavijayo rāmo gataśrīrvanagocaraḥ
vratī sthaṇḍilaśāyī ca śaṅke jīvati vā na vā
Rama has ceased from his endeavours for gaining victory. He has lost all his beauty, lives in the forest, is engaged in observances and always lies down on earth. I fear whether he is living still.

न हि वैदेहि रामस्त्वां द्रष्टुं वाप्युपलप्स्यते
पुरो बलाकैरसितैर्मेघैर्ज्योत्स्नामिवावृताम्

na hi vaidehi rāmastvāṁ draṣṭuṁ vāpyupalapsyate
puro balākairasitairmeghairjyotsnāmivāvṛtām

O Vaidehi, Rama shall not be able to see you like to the rays of the moon covered with blue clouds preceded by Balakas.* Raghava shall never get you back from my hands, like to Hiranyakasipu unable to regain his wife Kirti from Indra. *A kind of crane.

चारुस्मिते चारुदति चारुनेत्रे विलासिनि
मनो हरसि मे भीरु सुपर्णः पन्नगं यथा

cārusmite cārudati cārunetre vilāsini
mano harasi me bhīru suparṇaḥ pannagaṁ yathā
O you of beautiful teeth, O you having beautiful eyes, O sportive damsel, O timid one, you do steal my mind like to Garuda catching serpents.

क्लिष्टकौशेयवसनां तन्वीमप्यनलंकृताम्
तां दृष्ट्वा स्वेषु दारेषु रतिं नोपलभाम्यहम्

kliṣṭakauśeyavasanāṁ tanvīmapyanalaṁkṛtām
tāṁ dṛṣṭvā sveṣu dāreṣu ratiṁ nopalabhāmyaham
Beholding you, wearing a shattered silken cloth, slender and without any ornaments, I do not find any attachment in my own wives.

अन्तःपुरनिवासिन्यः स्त्रियः सर्वगुणान्विताः
यावन्त्यो मम सर्वासामैश्वर्यं कुरु जानकि

antaḥpuranivāsinyaḥ striyaḥ sarvaguṇānvitāḥ
yāvantyo mama sarvāsāmaiśvaryaṁ kuru jānaki
O daughter of Janaka, do you exercise, your supremacy, over all my wives, living in my seraglio and gifted with all accomplishments.

मम ह्यसितकेशान्ते त्रैलोक्यप्रवराः स्त्रियः
तास्त्वां परिचरिष्यन्ति श्रियमप्सरसो यथा

mama hyasitakeśānte trailokyapravarāḥ striyaḥ
tāstvāṁ paricariṣyanti śriyamapsaraso yathā
O you having black hair, all my wives are foremost in beauty over the three worlds. And they shall all attained you like to Apsaras waiting upon the Goddess of wealth.

यानि वैश्रवणे सुभ्रु रत्नानि च धनानि च
तानि लोकांश्च सुश्रोणि मां च भुङ्क्ष्व यथासुखम्

yāni vaiśravaṇe subhru ratnāni ca dhanāni ca
tāni lokāṁśca suśroṇi māṁ ca bhuṅkṣva yathāsukham
O you having beautiful eye brows and welldeveloped hips, do you, along with me, enjoy at your pleasure all the wealth and riches of Kubera. "The God of wealth or Pluto in Greak myth.

न रामस्तपसा देवि न बलेन न विक्रमैः
न धनेन मया तुल्यस्तेजसा यशसापि वा

na rāmastapasā devi na balena na vikramaiḥ
na dhanena mayā tulyastejasā yaśasāpi vā
O worshipful damsel, in asceticism, strength or prowess, wealth or fame, Rama is not my equal.

पिब विहर रमस्व भुङ्क्ष्व भोगा;न्धननिचयं प्रदिशामि मेदिनीं च
मयि लल ललने यथासुखं त्वं; त्वयि च समेत्य ललन्तु बान्धवास्ते

piba vihara ramasva bhuṅkṣva bhogā;ndhananicayaṁ pradiśāmi medinīṁ ca
mayi lala lalane yathāsukhaṁ tvaṁ; tvayi ca sametya lalantu bāndhavāste

Do you therefore at your pleasure drink, enjoy and eat. I shall confer on you wealth and the whole earth. Do you satisfy all your desires in me, O fair damsel, and let your friends be satisfied in you.

कुसुमिततरुजालसंततानि; भ्रमरयुतानि समुद्रतीरजानि
कनकविमलहारभूषिताङ्गी; विहर मया सह भीरु काननानि

kusumitatarujālasaṁtatāni; bhramarayutāni samudratīrajāni
kanakavimalahārabhūṣitāṅgī; vihara mayā saha bhīru kānanāni
And adorned with beautiful golden necklace, O timid lady, do you at your pleasure, range with me, in the forests, situated on the bank of the ocean, and filled with flowery trees and black bees. a

तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सीता रौद्रस्य रक्षसः
आर्ता दीनस्वरा दीनं प्रत्युवाच शनैर्वचः

tasya tadvacanaṁ śrutvā sītā raudrasya rakṣasaḥ
ārtā dīnasvarā dīnaṁ pratyuvāca śanairvacaḥ
Hearing those words of that terrible Raksasa, Sita, stricken with grief and of feeble voice, slowly replied.

दुःखार्ता रुदती सीता वेपमाना तपस्विनी
चिन्तयन्ती वरारोहा पतिमेव पतिव्रता

duḥkhārtā rudatī sītā vepamānā tapasvinī
cintayantī varārohā patimeva pativratā
Racked with grief, engaged in asceticism and weeping, Sita began. to tremble. And that excellent damsel, devoted to her husband, began to think of him.

तृणमन्तरतः कृत्वा प्रत्युवाच शुचिस्मिता
निवर्तय मनो मत्तः स्वजने क्रियतां मनः

tṛṇamantarataḥ kṛtvā pratyuvāca śucismitā
nivartaya mano mattaḥ svajane kriyatāṁ manaḥ
Placing a twig before, that one, of beautiful smile, said-"Do you take back your mind from me and place it in your own wives."

न मां प्रार्थयितुं युक्तस्त्वं सिद्धिमिव पापकृत्
अकार्यं न मया कार्यमेकपत्न्या विगर्हितम्
कुलं संप्राप्तया पुण्यं कुले महति जातया

na māṁ prārthayituṁ yuktastvaṁ siddhimiva pāpakṛt
akāryaṁ na mayā kāryamekapatnyā vigarhitam
kulaṁ saṁprāptayā puṇyaṁ kule mahati jātayā
Like to a sinner unworthy of praying for final emancipation, it dose not behove you to expect to come by me. Devoted to one husband I shall never perpetrate such an iniquitous act.

एवमुक्त्वा तु वैदेही रावणं तं यशस्विनी
राक्षसं पृष्ठतः कृत्वा भूयो वचनमब्रवीत्

evamuktvā tu vaidehī rāvaṇaṁ taṁ yaśasvinī
rākṣasaṁ pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā bhūyo vacanamabravīt

I am born in a high and have been married in a pious family. Having accosted Ravana thus, the well-known Vaidehi, turning her back, again spake to him, saying. "I should not live with you since I am another's wife and chaste."

नाहमौपयिकी भार्या परभार्या सती तव
साधु धर्ममवेक्षस्व साधु साधुव्रतं चर

nāhamaupayikī bhāryā parabhāryā satī tava
sādhu dharmamavekṣasva sādhu sādhuvrataṁ cara
Have your eyes always on religion and do you follow in the track of piety. Like to yours own wives, others are worthy of being protected by you, O ranger of the night.

अतुष्टं स्वेषु दारेषु चपलं चलितेन्द्रियम्
नयन्ति निकृतिप्रज्ञां परदाराः पराभवम्

atuṣṭaṁ sveṣu dāreṣu capalaṁ calitendriyam
nayanti nikṛtiprajñāṁ paradārāḥ parābhavam

Making an example of you, do you enjoy with your own wives. Forsooth those vicious-minded, those of agitated senses, who are not satisfied with their own wives, are brought to misery by others' wives.

इह सन्तो न वा सन्ति सतो वा नानुवर्तसे
वचो मिथ्या प्रणीतात्मा पथ्यमुक्तं विचक्षणैः

iha santo na vā santi sato vā nānuvartase
vaco mithyā praṇītātmā pathyamuktaṁ vicakṣaṇaiḥ
Or the considerate people have spoken the truth, but you, for the destruction of the race of the Raksasas, considering that false, had not followed it.

अकृतात्मानमासाद्य राजानमनये रतम्
समृद्धानि विनश्यन्ति राष्ट्राणि नगराणि च

akṛtātmānamāsādya rājānamanaye ratam
samṛddhāni vinaśyanti rāṣṭrāṇi nagarāṇi ca
Wealth, kingdom and cities-all are brought to naught when they are placed at the hands of a vicious and illiterate king.

तथेयं त्वां समासाद्य लङ्का रत्नौघ संकुला
अपराधात्तवैकस्य नचिराद्विनशिष्यति

tatheyaṁ tvāṁ samāsādya laṅkā ratnaugha saṁkulā
aparādhāttavaikasya nacirādvinaśiṣyati
Obtaining you, (therefore) as her king and for your folly only, this city of Lanka, abounding in jewels, shall soon be ruined.

स्वकृतैर्हन्यमानस्य रावणादीर्घदर्शिनः
अभिनन्दन्ति भूतानि विनाशे पापकर्मणः

svakṛtairhanyamānasya rāvaṇādīrghadarśinaḥ
abhinandanti bhūtāni vināśe pāpakarmaṇaḥ
O Ravana, every one delight in the destruction of that inconsiderate being, who bring about his own destruction and is engaged in the perpetration of evil deeds.

एवं त्वां पापकर्माणं वक्ष्यन्ति निकृता जनाः
दिष्ट्यैतद्व्यसनं प्राप्तो रौद्र इत्येव हर्षिताः

evaṁ tvāṁ pāpakarmāṇaṁ vakṣyanti nikṛtā janāḥ
diṣṭyaitadvyasanaṁ prāpto raudra ityeva harṣitāḥ

In this way, yourself, the perpetrator of vicious acts, meeting with your end, those persons who had been tyrannised by you, shall, delightedly, say, “Oh! blessed are we since this terrible (Raksasa) has met with his end."

शक्या लोभयितुं नाहमैश्वर्येण धनेन वा
अनन्या राघवेणाहं भास्करेण प्रभा यथा

śakyā lobhayituṁ nāhamaiśvaryeṇa dhanena vā
ananyā rāghaveṇāhaṁ bhāskareṇa prabhā yathā
With wealth or riches you shall not be able to tempt me. As the rays of the sun belong to him, so I am Raghava's only.

उपधाय भुजं तस्य लोकनाथस्य सत्कृतम्
कथं नामोपधास्यामि भुजमन्यस्य कस्यचित्

upadhāya bhujaṁ tasya lokanāthasya satkṛtam
kathaṁ nāmopadhāsyāmi bhujamanyasya kasyacit
Having laid my head on the beautiful arms of that lord of men, how shall I place it again on another's?

अहमौपयिकी भार्या तस्यैव वसुधापतेः
व्रतस्नातस्य विप्रस्य विद्येव विदितात्मनः

ahamaupayikī bhāryā tasyaiva vasudhāpateḥ
vratasnātasya viprasya vidyeva viditātmanaḥ
Like the knowledge of one God monopolized by the Brahmanas only, I am the spouse of that lord of earth only, cognisant of higher truths and marrying me according to the pious ceremonials.

साधु रावण रामेण मां समानय दुःखिताम्
वने वाशितया सार्धं करेण्वेव गजाधिपम्

sādhu rāvaṇa rāmeṇa māṁ samānaya duḥkhitām
vane vāśitayā sārdhaṁ kareṇveva gajādhipam
to May good betide you, O Ravana. Do you take me to Rama, stricken with grief as I am, like to a she-elephant anxiously waiting in the forest brought to the lord of elephants.

मित्रमौपयिकं कर्तुं रामः स्थानं परीप्सता
वधं चानिच्छता घोरं त्वयासौ पुरुषर्षभः

mitramaupayikaṁ kartuṁ rāmaḥ sthānaṁ parīpsatā
vadhaṁ cānicchatā ghoraṁ tvayāsau puruṣarṣabhaḥ
It behove you to make friends with Rama, that best of men, if do you desire to maintain your empire and do not wish to bring about your own destruction.

वर्जयेद्वज्रमुत्सृष्टं वर्जयेदन्तकश्चिरम्
त्वद्विधं न तु संक्रुद्धो लोकनाथः स राघवः

varjayedvajramutsṛṣṭaṁ varjayedantakaściram
tvadvidhaṁ na tu saṁkruddho lokanāthaḥ sa rāghavaḥ
Thunderbolt, even, when hurled, may leave you, Death himself may overlook you-but there is no safety for you, if Raghava, the lord of men is enraged.

रामस्य धनुषः शब्दं श्रोष्यसि त्वं महास्वनम्
शतक्रतुविसृष्टस्य निर्घोषमशनेरिव

rāmasya dhanuṣaḥ śabdaṁ śroṣyasi tvaṁ mahāsvanam
śatakratuvisṛṣṭasya nirghoṣamaśaneriva

You shall hear the terrible sound of the twang of Rama's bow, like to the sound of the thunderbolt hurled by Indra. Soon shall arrows, bearing the names of Rama and Laksmana and having fiery heads like those of snakes, alight here.

रक्षांसि परिनिघ्नन्तः पुर्यामस्यां समन्ततः
असंपातं करिष्यन्ति पतन्तः कङ्कवाससः

rakṣāṁsi parinighnantaḥ puryāmasyāṁ samantataḥ
asaṁpātaṁ kariṣyanti patantaḥ kaṅkavāsasaḥ
And covered with Kanka leaves they shall undoubtedly cover the whole city and devastate it by destroying all the Raksasas.

राक्षसेन्द्रमहासर्पान्स रामगरुडो महान्
उद्धरिष्यति वेगेन वैनतेय इवोरगान्

rākṣasendramahāsarpānsa rāmagaruḍo mahān
uddhariṣyati vegena vainateya ivoragān
Like to Garuda pulling up the snakes, the Garuda like Rama shall pull up your snake-like Raksasas.

अपनेष्यति मां भर्ता त्वत्तः शीघ्रमरिंदमः
असुरेभ्यः श्रियं दीप्तां विष्णुस्त्रिभिरिव क्रमैः

apaneṣyati māṁ bhartā tvattaḥ śīghramariṁdamaḥ
asurebhyaḥ śriyaṁ dīptāṁ viṣṇustribhiriva kramaiḥ

Like to Visnu recovering the effulgent Sri (the Goddess of wealth) from the Asuras, by crossing over the three worlds with three foot-steps, my husband, the conqueror of foes, shall recover me from you.

जनस्थाने हतस्थाने निहते रक्षसां बले
अशक्तेन त्वया रक्षः कृतमेतदसाधु वै

janasthāne hatasthāne nihate rakṣasāṁ bale
aśaktena tvayā rakṣaḥ kṛtametadasādhu vai
Janasthana has been devastated, the host of Raksasas has been killed, and you had been disabled. Truly you had perpetrated an impious deed.

न हि गन्धमुपाघ्राय रामलक्ष्मणयोस्त्वया
शक्यं संदर्शने स्थातुं शुना शार्दूलयोरिव

na hi gandhamupāghrāya rāmalakṣmaṇayostvayā
śakyaṁ saṁdarśane sthātuṁ śunā śārdūlayoriva

O Raksasa, those two lions among men going out to enquire about the illusive deer, I was ravished by you, entering the empty hermitage O vile wight. And like to a dog incapable of standing before a tiger, it would have been impossible for you, to wait there in the presence of Rama and Laksmana.

तस्य ते विग्रहे ताभ्यां युगग्रहणमस्थिरम्
वृत्रस्येवेन्द्रबाहुभ्यां बाहोरेकस्य निग्रहः

tasya te vigrahe tābhyāṁ yugagrahaṇamasthiram
vṛtrasyevendrabāhubhyāṁ bāhorekasya nigrahaḥ

If do you engage in conflict with them, your wealth and friends shall be of no avail to you (and you shall be discomfited) like to onehanded Asura Vstra by the two handed Indra.* *The allusion is-the mighty Asura Vrtra fought with Indra for a long time even after he had his one hand chopped off.

क्षिप्रं तव स नाथो मे रामः सौमित्रिणा सह
तोयमल्पमिवादित्यः प्राणानादास्यते शरैः

kṣipraṁ tava sa nātho me rāmaḥ saumitriṇā saha
toyamalpamivādityaḥ prāṇānādāsyate śaraiḥ
Soon shall my husband, with the assistance of Laksmana, draw out your life with arrows, like to the sun drying up, by his rays, shallow water.

गिरिं कुबेरस्य गतोऽथ वालयं; सभां गतो वा वरुणस्य राज्ञः
असंशयं दाशरथेर्न मोक्ष्यसे; महाद्रुमः कालहतोऽशनेरिव

giriṁ kuberasya gato'tha vālayaṁ; sabhāṁ gato vā varuṇasya rājñaḥ
asaṁśayaṁ dāśaratherna mokṣyase; mahādrumaḥ kālahato'śaneriva

Whether do you repair to the abode of Kubera, or whether do you, terrified, take refuge to the assembly of Varuna, you shall, for certain, be destroyed by the son of Dasaratha, like to a mighty tree broken down by thunderbolt.

सीताया वचनं श्रुत्वा परुषं राक्षसाधिपः
प्रत्युवाच ततः सीतां विप्रियं प्रियदर्शनाम्

sītāyā vacanaṁ śrutvā paruṣaṁ rākṣasādhipaḥ
pratyuvāca tataḥ sītāṁ vipriyaṁ priyadarśanām
Hearing those harsh accents, that lord of Raksasas, replied to Sita, of comely presence, with the following unpleasant words.

यथा यथा सान्त्वयिता वश्यः स्त्रीणां तथा तथा
यथा यथा प्रियं वक्ता परिभूतस्तथा तथा

yathā yathā sāntvayitā vaśyaḥ strīṇāṁ tathā tathā
yathā yathā priyaṁ vaktā paribhūtastathā tathā

It is generally found on earth that the more a woman is courted by a man, the more she is brought under his influence, (But for you) the more kindly I have been behaving towards you, the more roughly I have been treated.

संनियच्छति मे क्रोधं त्वयि कामः समुत्थितः
द्रवतो मार्गमासाद्य हयानिव सुसारथिः

saṁniyacchati me krodhaṁ tvayi kāmaḥ samutthitaḥ
dravato mārgamāsādya hayāniva susārathiḥ
Truly dose my love for you keep in control the wrath like to a good charioteer restraining the swerving steed.

वामः कामो मनुष्याणां यस्मिन्किल निबध्यते
जने तस्मिंस्त्वनुक्रोशः स्नेहश्च किल जायते

vāmaḥ kāmo manuṣyāṇāṁ yasminkila nibadhyate
jane tasmiṁstvanukrośaḥ snehaśca kila jāyate
O mighty is amour to men, for on whom this amour fall, albeit she is an object of wrath, becomes an object of kindness and affection.

एतस्मात्कारणान्न तां घतयामि वरानने
वधार्हामवमानार्हां मिथ्याप्रव्रजिते रताम्

etasmātkāraṇānna tāṁ ghatayāmi varānane
vadhārhāmavamānārhāṁ mithyāpravrajite ratām
O you of fair countenance, it is for this reason, that I do not destroy you, although you, who are engaged in false asceticism, are worthy of being killed and dishonoured. do you

परुषाणि हि वाक्यानि यानि यानि ब्रवीषि माम्
तेषु तेषु वधो युक्तस्तव मैथिलि दारुणः

paruṣāṇi hi vākyāni yāni yāni bravīṣi mām
teṣu teṣu vadho yuktastava maithili dāruṇaḥ
O Maithili, for each and every one of all those harsh words which you had used by me, deserve death.

एवमुक्त्वा तु वैदेहीं रावणो राक्षसाधिपः
क्रोधसंरम्भसंयुक्तः सीतामुत्तरमब्रवीत्

evamuktvā tu vaidehīṁ rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ
krodhasaṁrambhasaṁyuktaḥ sītāmuttaramabravīt
Having spoken thus to Vaidehi, Ravana, the lord of Raksasas, having his wrath subdued, again bespake Sita.

द्वौ मासौ रक्षितव्यौ मे योऽवधिस्ते मया कृतः
ततः शयनमारोह मम त्वं वरवर्णिनि

dvau māsau rakṣitavyau me yo'vadhiste mayā kṛtaḥ
tataḥ śayanamāroha mama tvaṁ varavarṇini
I shall wait for those two months, of which I have made a contract, after which you shall have to share my bed. O you of a comely presence.

द्वाभ्यामूर्ध्वं तु मासाभ्यां भर्तारं मामनिच्छतीम्
मम त्वां प्रातराशार्थमारभन्ते महानसे

dvābhyāmūrdhvaṁ tu māsābhyāṁ bhartāraṁ māmanicchatīm
mama tvāṁ prātarāśārthamārabhante mahānase
Even then if you do refuse to regard me as your husband, my cooks shall mince your limbs with steel and serve you for my morning meal.

तां तर्ज्यमानां संप्रेक्ष्य राक्षसेन्द्रेण जानकीम्
देवगन्धर्वकन्यास्ता विषेदुर्विपुलेक्षणाः

tāṁ tarjyamānāṁ saṁprekṣya rākṣasendreṇa jānakīm
devagandharvakanyāstā viṣedurvipulekṣaṇāḥ
Beholding the lord of Raksasas remonstrate with the daughter of Janaka is this wise, the daughters of the celestials and Gandharvas became exceedingly sorry.

ओष्ठप्रकारैरपरा नेत्रवक्त्रैस्तथापराः
सीतामाश्वासयामासुस्तर्जितां तेन रक्षसा

oṣṭhaprakārairaparā netravaktraistathāparāḥ
sītāmāśvāsayāmāsustarjitāṁ tena rakṣasā
Some with lips, some with eyes, and some with gestures of their faces, they all consoled Sita, thus distressed by that Raksasa.

ताभिराश्वासिता सीता रावणं राक्षसाधिपम्
उवाचात्महितं वाक्यं वृत्तशौण्डीर्यगर्वितम्

tābhirāśvāsitā sītā rāvaṇaṁ rākṣasādhipam
uvācātmahitaṁ vākyaṁ vṛttaśauṇḍīryagarvitam
Thus consoled by them, and being proud of her good conduct and her husband's heroism, Sita thus addressed Ravana, the lord of Raksasas.

नूनं न ते जनः कश्चिदसिन्निःश्रेयसे स्थितः
निवारयति यो न त्वां कर्मणोऽस्माद्विगर्हितात्

nūnaṁ na te janaḥ kaścidasinniḥśreyase sthitaḥ
nivārayati yo na tvāṁ karmaṇo'smādvigarhitāt
Forsooth there is no person in this city who desire your welfare and therefore prevent you from such an impious deed.

मां हि धर्मात्मनः पत्नीं शचीमिव शचीपतेः
त्वदन्यस्त्रिषु लोकेषु प्रार्थयेन्मनसापि कः

māṁ hi dharmātmanaḥ patnīṁ śacīmiva śacīpateḥ
tvadanyastriṣu lokeṣu prārthayenmanasāpi kaḥ
Who is there in the three worlds, who even desire me in mind, who am the spouse of the virtuous souled (Rama) like to Indra's Saci.

राक्षसाधम रामस्य भार्याममिततेजसः
उक्तवानसि यत्पापं क्व गतस्तस्य मोक्ष्यसे

rākṣasādhama rāmasya bhāryāmamitatejasaḥ
uktavānasi yatpāpaṁ kva gatastasya mokṣyase
O you the vilest of the Raksasas, for using those vicious words towards the spouse of Rama, of immeasured prowess, repairing whither shall you escape vengeance?

यथा दृप्तश्च मातङ्गः शशश्च सहितौ वने
तथा द्विरदवद्रामस्त्वं नीच शशवत्स्मृतः

yathā dṛptaśca mātaṅgaḥ śaśaśca sahitau vane
tathā dviradavadrāmastvaṁ nīca śaśavatsmṛtaḥ
Like to an infuriated elephant encountering a hare in the forest, you shall O Vile! a hare as you are, meet with that elephant-like Rama.

स त्वमिक्ष्वाकुनाथं वै क्षिपन्निह न लज्जसे
चक्षुषो विषयं तस्य न तावदुपगच्छसि

sa tvamikṣvākunāthaṁ vai kṣipanniha na lajjase
cakṣuṣo viṣayaṁ tasya na tāvadupagacchasi
You are not ashamed of railing that lord of Iksvakus, so long as dose you not come within his ken.

इमे ते नयने क्रूरे विरूपे कृष्णपिङ्गले
क्षितौ न पतिते कस्मान्मामनार्यनिरीक्षितः

ime te nayane krūre virūpe kṛṣṇapiṅgale
kṣitau na patite kasmānmāmanāryanirīkṣitaḥ
O base! why do not your grim, terrible, coppery eyes, looking so viciously at me, fall down on earth.

तस्य धर्मात्मनः पत्नीं स्नुषां दशरथस्य च
कथं व्याहरतो मां ते न जिह्वा पाप शीर्यते

tasya dharmātmanaḥ patnīṁ snuṣāṁ daśarathasya ca
kathaṁ vyāharato māṁ te na jihvā pāpa śīryate
O vicious wretch, I am the spouse of that virtuous-souled (Rama) and daughter-in-law of Dasaratha—using these vile words towards me, why dose not your tongue fall off?

असंदेशात्तु रामस्य तपसश्चानुपालनात्
न त्वां कुर्मि दशग्रीव भस्म भस्मार्हतेजसा

asaṁdeśāttu rāmasya tapasaścānupālanāt
na tvāṁ kurmi daśagrīva bhasma bhasmārhatejasā
O Ten-necked one, I can instantly reduce you to ashes but for Rama's mandate and my ascetic observances.

नापहर्तुमहं शक्या तस्य रामस्य धीमतः
विधिस्तव वधार्थाय विहितो नात्र संशयः

nāpahartumahaṁ śakyā tasya rāmasya dhīmataḥ
vidhistava vadhārthāya vihito nātra saṁśayaḥ
You could not have ravished me in the presence of the highly intelligent Rama. And undoubtedly for your destruction this has been brought about by God.

शूरेण धनदभ्राता बलैः समुदितेन च
अपोह्य रामं कस्माद्धि दारचौर्यं त्वया कृतम्

śūreṇa dhanadabhrātā balaiḥ samuditena ca
apohya rāmaṁ kasmāddhi dāracauryaṁ tvayā kṛtam
You are heroic and Kubera's brother and great in prowess, why didst you then take me by stealth after despatching Rama away from the hermitage?”

सीताया वचनं श्रुत्वा रावणो राक्षसाधिपः
विवृत्य नयने क्रूरे जानकीमन्ववैक्षत

sītāyā vacanaṁ śrutvā rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ
vivṛtya nayane krūre jānakīmanvavaikṣata
Hearing those words of Sita, Ravana, the lord of Raksasas, whirling his grim eyes, looked towards the daughter of Janaka.

नीलजीमूतसंकाशो महाभुजशिरोधरः
सिंहसत्त्वगतिः श्रीमान्दीप्तजिह्वोग्रलोचनः

nīlajīmūtasaṁkāśo mahābhujaśirodharaḥ
siṁhasattvagatiḥ śrīmāndīptajihvogralocanaḥ
He was like to a mass of blue clouds and his arms and necks were long and spacious. He was gifted with elephantine gaits and his tongues and eyes were sharp and flaming.

चलाग्रमकुटः प्रांशुश्चित्रमाल्यानुलेपनः
रक्तमाल्याम्बरधरस्तप्ताङ्गदविभूषणः

calāgramakuṭaḥ prāṁśuścitramālyānulepanaḥ
raktamālyāmbaradharastaptāṅgadavibhūṣaṇaḥ

The top of his crown was shaking and he had charming garland around his neck and his person sprinkled with paste. He had crimson-coloured garlands and clothes on and his charming arms were adorned with ornaments. Encircled with a sword-belt around his waist he appeared like to Mandara, entwined by a snake at the time of the churning of the ocean.

तरुणादित्यवर्णाभ्यां कुण्डलाभ्यां विभूषितः
रक्तपल्लवपुष्पाभ्यामशोकाभ्यामिवाचलः

taruṇādityavarṇābhyāṁ kuṇḍalābhyāṁ vibhūṣitaḥ
raktapallavapuṣpābhyāmaśokābhyāmivācalaḥ
And adorned with a pair of Kundalas (A kind of ornament worn on ears.) resembling the newly risen Sun he looked like a hill covered with two Asoka trees enveloped with crimson flowers and leaves.

अवेक्षमाणो वैदेहीं कोपसंरक्तलोचनः
उवाच रावणः सीतां भुजंग इव निःश्वसन्

avekṣamāṇo vaidehīṁ kopasaṁraktalocanaḥ
uvāca rāvaṇaḥ sītāṁ bhujaṁga iva niḥśvasan
And having his eyes red hot with ire, sighing again and again like to a snake and casting his looks upon Sita, Ravana addressed her again, saying.

अनयेनाभिसंपन्नमर्थहीनमनुव्रते
नाशयाम्यहमद्य त्वां सूर्यः संध्यामिवौजसा

anayenābhisaṁpannamarthahīnamanuvrate
nāśayāmyahamadya tvāṁ sūryaḥ saṁdhyāmivaujasā
O you following asceticism, this your vow is without any meaning and beyond the pale of morality. Even shall I destroy you today like to the Sun dispelling darkness with his rays.

इत्युक्त्वा मैथिलीं राजा रावणः शत्रुरावणः
संदिदेश ततः सर्वा राक्षसीर्घोरदर्शनाः

ityuktvā maithilīṁ rājā rāvaṇaḥ śatrurāvaṇaḥ
saṁdideśa tataḥ sarvā rākṣasīrghoradarśanāḥ
Having thus addressed Maithili, the inimical king Ravana cast his looks towards the grimvisaged Raksasis.

इति प्रतिसमादिश्य राक्षसेन्द्रः पुनः पुनः
काममन्युपरीतात्मा जानकीं पर्यतर्जयत्

iti pratisamādiśya rākṣasendraḥ punaḥ punaḥ
kāmamanyuparītātmā jānakīṁ paryatarjayat
And having ordered thus again and again, that lord of Raksasas, stricken with amour and ire, addressed Sita, roaring fiercely.

उपगम्य ततः क्षिप्रं राक्षसी धान्यमालिनी
परिष्वज्य दशग्रीवमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्

upagamya tataḥ kṣipraṁ rākṣasī dhānyamālinī
pariṣvajya daśagrīvamidaṁ vacanamabravīt
Thereupon approaching speedily and embracing the Ten-necked one, one Raksasi named Dhanyamalini bespoke him.

मया क्रीड महाराजसीतया किं तवानया
अकामां कामयानस्य शरीरमुपतप्यते
इच्छन्तीं कामयानस्य प्रीतिर्भवति शोभना

mayā krīḍa mahārājasītayā kiṁ tavānayā
akāmāṁ kāmayānasya śarīramupatapyate
icchantīṁ kāmayānasya prītirbhavati śobhanā
