मधून्यचिन्तयित्वेमान्भक्षयन्ति पिबन्ति च

ebhiḥ pradharṣitāścaiva vāritā vanarakṣibhiḥ
madhūnyacintayitvemānbhakṣayanti pibanti ca
I prevented them along with these attendants, but disregarding me, they drank and feasted there at their pleasure.

शिष्टमत्रापविध्यन्ति भक्षयन्ति तथापरे
निवार्यमाणास्ते सर्वे भ्रुवौ वै दर्शयन्ति हि

śiṣṭamatrāpavidhyanti bhakṣayanti tathāpare
nivāryamāṇāste sarve bhruvau vai darśayanti hi
Some of them went beyond the pale of food conduct, others ate at their pleasure, and all frowned (at us).

इमे हि संरब्धतरास्तथा तैः संप्रधर्षिताः
वारयन्तो वनात्तस्मात्क्रुद्धैर्वानरपुंगवैः

ime hi saṁrabdhatarāstathā taiḥ saṁpradharṣitāḥ
vārayanto vanāttasmātkruddhairvānarapuṁgavaiḥ
When these attendants, being insulted by them, were greatly wroth, they were driven out of the garden, by those powerful and enraged monkeys.

ततस्तैर्बहुभिर्वीरैर्वानरैर्वानरर्षभाः
संरक्तनयनैः क्रोधाद्धरयः संप्रचालिताः

tatastairbahubhirvīrairvānarairvānararṣabhāḥ
saṁraktanayanaiḥ krodhāddharayaḥ saṁpracālitāḥ
They were greatly assailed by those many thousand heroic monkeys, worked up with ire and having reddened eyes.

पाणिभिर्निहताः केचित्केचिज्जानुभिराहताः
प्रकृष्टाश्च यथाकामं देवमार्गं च दर्शिताः

pāṇibhirnihatāḥ kecitkecijjānubhirāhatāḥ
prakṛṣṭāśca yathākāmaṁ devamārgaṁ ca darśitāḥ
Some had their arins broken, some had their knee-joints crushed and some of them were thrown up in the sky.

एवमेते हताः शूरास्त्वयि तिष्ठति भर्तरि
कृत्स्नं मधुवनं चैव प्रकामं तैः प्रभक्ष्यते

evamete hatāḥ śūrāstvayi tiṣṭhati bhartari
kṛtsnaṁ madhuvanaṁ caiva prakāmaṁ taiḥ prabhakṣyate
Yourself their lord living, these heroes are beaten, and the entire Madhuvana is being freely enjoyed by them.

एवं विज्ञाप्यमानं तु सुग्रीवं वानरर्षभम्
अपृच्छत्तं महाप्राज्ञो लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा

evaṁ vijñāpyamānaṁ tu sugrīvaṁ vānararṣabham
apṛcchattaṁ mahāprājño lakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā
The highly intelligent Laksmana, the slayer of foes, addressed Sugriva, the foremost O the monkeys, while he was thus being informed, saying.

किमयं वानरो राजन्वनपः प्रत्युपस्थितः
कं चार्थमभिनिर्दिश्य दुःखितो वाक्यमब्रवीत्

kimayaṁ vānaro rājanvanapaḥ pratyupasthitaḥ
kaṁ cārthamabhinirdiśya duḥkhito vākyamabravīt
O king, why has this monkey, the guard over the forest, come to you, and what sorrow has led him to give vent to these expressions?

एवमुक्तस्तु सुग्रीवो लक्ष्मणेन महात्मना
लक्ष्मणं प्रत्युवाचेदं वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः

evamuktastu sugrīvo lakṣmaṇena mahātmanā
lakṣmaṇaṁ pratyuvācedaṁ vākyaṁ vākyaviśāradaḥ
Being thus addressed by the high-souled Laksmana, Sugriva, skilled in the art of speech, replied.

आर्य लक्ष्मण संप्राह वीरो दधिमुखः कपिः
अङ्गदप्रमुखैर्वीरैर्भक्षितं मधुवानरैः

ārya lakṣmaṇa saṁprāha vīro dadhimukhaḥ kapiḥ
aṅgadapramukhairvīrairbhakṣitaṁ madhuvānaraiḥ
O worshipful Laksmana, the heroic monkey Dadhimukha speaks that the war-like monkeys headed by Angada have drunk honey.

नैषामकृतकृत्यानामीदृशः स्यादुपक्रमः
वनं यथाभिपन्नं तैः साधितं कर्म वानरैः

naiṣāmakṛtakṛtyānāmīdṛśaḥ syādupakramaḥ
vanaṁ yathābhipannaṁ taiḥ sādhitaṁ karma vānaraiḥ
They would not have engaged in such an unfair proceeding had they been unsuccessful in their mission. They have surely achieved success while they have thus been bent upon devastating the orchard.

कार्यसिद्धिर्हनुमति मतिश्च हरिपुंगव
व्यवसायश्च वीर्यं च श्रुतं चापि प्रतिष्ठितम्

kāryasiddhirhanumati matiśca haripuṁgava
vyavasāyaśca vīryaṁ ca śrutaṁ cāpi pratiṣṭhitam

There is none else but Hanuman who is the instrumental of this work, for that best of monkeys has in him a high intellect, know the art of success, is gifted with courage, strength and prowess and is conversant with Sastras.

आगतैश्च प्रविष्टं तद्यथा मधुवनं हि तैः
धर्षितं च वनं कृत्स्नमुपयुक्तं च वानरैः
वारिताः सहिताः पालास्तथा जानुभिराहताः

āgataiśca praviṣṭaṁ tadyathā madhuvanaṁ hi taiḥ
dharṣitaṁ ca vanaṁ kṛtsnamupayuktaṁ ca vānaraiḥ
vāritāḥ sahitāḥ pālāstathā jānubhirāhatāḥ

Forsooth that orchard has been laid waste by these heroes headed by Angada. And ransacking the southern quarter, those leading monkeys have come back and delightedly entered the Madhuvana. And the whole orchard has been explored and enjoyed by those monkeys and the attendants beaten and wounded on their kneejoints. To communicate to me this intelligence, this monkey of known prowess, and sweet accents, named Dhadimukha, has come here.

दृष्टा सीता महाबाहो सौमित्रे पश्य तत्त्वतः
अभिगम्य यथा सर्वे पिबन्ति मधु वानराः

dṛṣṭā sītā mahābāho saumitre paśya tattvataḥ
abhigamya yathā sarve pibanti madhu vānarāḥ
O you of mighty arms, O son of Sumitra, forsooth they have beheld Sita, since the monkeys, just on their return, have engaged in drinking honey.

न चाप्यदृष्ट्वा वैदेहीं विश्रुताः पुरुषर्षभ
वनं दात्त वरं दिव्यं धर्षयेयुर्वनौकसः

na cāpyadṛṣṭvā vaidehīṁ viśrutāḥ puruṣarṣabha
vanaṁ dātta varaṁ divyaṁ dharṣayeyurvanaukasaḥ
O best of men, they are all well-known monkeys and without espying Vaidehi they would not have engaged in the destruction of that orchard conferred on us as a gift by the celestials.

ततः प्रहृष्टो धर्मात्मा लक्ष्मणः सहराघवः
श्रुत्वा कर्णसुखां वाणीं सुग्रीववदनाच्च्युताम्

tataḥ prahṛṣṭo dharmātmā lakṣmaṇaḥ saharāghavaḥ
śrutvā karṇasukhāṁ vāṇīṁ sugrīvavadanāccyutām
Hearing these words from Sugriva, pleasant to ears, the virtuous-souled Laksmana along with Raghava, was greatly pleased.

प्राहृष्यत भृशं रामो लक्ष्मणश्च महायशाः
श्रुत्वा दधिमुखस्येदं सुग्रीवस्तु प्रहृष्य च
वनपालं पुनर्वाक्यं सुग्रीवः प्रत्यभाषत

prāhṛṣyata bhṛśaṁ rāmo lakṣmaṇaśca mahāyaśāḥ
śrutvā dadhimukhasyedaṁ sugrīvastu prahṛṣya ca
vanapālaṁ punarvākyaṁ sugrīvaḥ pratyabhāṣata
And hearing this from Dadhimukha, Sugriva, greatly gratified; addressed that lord of the for st, gain, Saying.

प्रीतोऽस्मि सौम्य यद्भुक्तं वनं तैः कृतकर्मभिः
मर्षितं मर्षणीयं च चेष्टितं कृतकर्मणाम्

prīto'smi saumya yadbhuktaṁ vanaṁ taiḥ kṛtakarmabhiḥ
marṣitaṁ marṣaṇīyaṁ ca ceṣṭitaṁ kṛtakarmaṇām

Greatly pleased I am, since, they, being successful, have explored this forest. And the insulting procedure of the successful is also pardonable. Do you soon go there and protect that orchards, and send here all those monkeys headed by Hanuman.

इच्छामि शीघ्रं हनुमत्प्रधाना;न्शाखामृगांस्तान्मृगराजदर्पान्
द्रष्टुं कृतार्थान्सह राघवाभ्यां; श्रोतुं च सीताधिगमे प्रयत्नम्

icchāmi śīghraṁ hanumatpradhānā;nśākhāmṛgāṁstānmṛgarājadarpān
draṣṭuṁ kṛtārthānsaha rāghavābhyāṁ; śrotuṁ ca sītādhigame prayatnam
Along with these two descendants of Raghu, I long to know soon from these monkeys headed by Hanuman, and proud like lions, what they have settled for the regaining of Sita.

सुग्रीवेणैवमुक्तस्तु हृष्टो दधिमुखः कपिः
राघवं लक्ष्मणं चैव सुग्रीवं चाभ्यवादयत्

sugrīveṇaivamuktastu hṛṣṭo dadhimukhaḥ kapiḥ
rāghavaṁ lakṣmaṇaṁ caiva sugrīvaṁ cābhyavādayat
Being thus addressed by Sugriva, the monkey Dadhimuklia, delighted, bowed to him, Raghava and Laksmana.

स प्रणम्य च सुग्रीवं राघवौ च महाबलौ
वानरैः सहितैः शूरैर्दिवमेवोत्पपात ह

sa praṇamya ca sugrīvaṁ rāghavau ca mahābalau
vānaraiḥ sahitaiḥ śūrairdivamevotpapāta ha
And adoring Sugriva and the highly powerful descendants of Raghu, he along with other heroic monkeys, leaped up in the sky.

स यथैवागतः पूर्वं तथैव त्वरितो गतः
निपत्य गगनाद्भूमौ तद्वनं प्रविवेश ह

sa yathaivāgataḥ pūrvaṁ tathaiva tvarito gataḥ
nipatya gaganādbhūmau tadvanaṁ praviveśa ha
He went away with the same speed with which he came and leaping down on the earth from the sky, entered the orchard.

स प्रविष्टो मधुवनं ददर्श हरियूथपान्
विमदानुद्धतान्सर्वान्मेहमानान्मधूदकम्

sa praviṣṭo madhuvanaṁ dadarśa hariyūthapān
vimadānuddhatānsarvānmehamānānmadhūdakam
And entering that forest he beheld all the leaders of the monkeys spending the hours delightedly, having passed urine, the outcome of honey.

स तानुपागमद्वीरो बद्ध्वा करपुटाञ्जलिम्
उवाच वचनं श्लक्ष्णमिदं हृष्टवदङ्गदम्

sa tānupāgamadvīro baddhvā karapuṭāñjalim
uvāca vacanaṁ ślakṣṇamidaṁ hṛṣṭavadaṅgadam
And approaching them, the hero, with folded hands and delighted, addressed Angada, with the following words.

सौम्य रोषो न कर्तव्यो यदेभिरभिवारितः
अज्ञानाद्रक्षिभिः क्रोधाद्भवन्तः प्रतिषेधिताः

saumya roṣo na kartavyo yadebhirabhivāritaḥ
ajñānādrakṣibhiḥ krodhādbhavantaḥ pratiṣedhitāḥ
O gentle one, do you not take offence, for these monkeys, protecting the garden enraged, unwittingly prevented you.

युवराजस्त्वमीशश्च वनस्यास्य महाबल
मौर्ख्यात्पूर्वं कृतो दोषस्तद्भवान्क्षन्तुमर्हति

yuvarājastvamīśaśca vanasyāsya mahābala
maurkhyātpūrvaṁ kṛto doṣastadbhavānkṣantumarhati
O you of great strength, you are worn out with your long journey, do you drink your own honey, you are our prince and the master of this garden.

यथैव हि पिता तेऽभूत्पूर्वं हरिगणेश्वरः
तथा त्वमपि सुग्रीवो नान्यस्तु हरिसत्तम

yathaiva hi pitā te'bhūtpūrvaṁ harigaṇeśvaraḥ
tathā tvamapi sugrīvo nānyastu harisattama
It behove you to forgive us for our wrath arising out of ignorance. Like to your sire before, yourself and Sugriva are the lords of these monkey hosts, O you foremost of them and none else.

आख्यातं हि मया गत्वा पितृव्यस्य तवानघ
इहोपयानं सर्वेषामेतेषां वनचारिणाम्

ākhyātaṁ hi mayā gatvā pitṛvyasya tavānagha
ihopayānaṁ sarveṣāmeteṣāṁ vanacāriṇām

O innocent prince, I have related all about this to your uncle. When I described to him, the arrival of all these forest rangers, as well as of yours accompanied by them, and the destruction of this garden by you all, he was not the least offended, rather delighted.

प्रहृष्टो मां पितृव्यस्ते सुग्रीवो वानरेश्वरः
शीघ्रं प्रेषय सर्वांस्तानिति होवाच पार्थिवः

prahṛṣṭo māṁ pitṛvyaste sugrīvo vānareśvaraḥ
śīghraṁ preṣaya sarvāṁstāniti hovāca pārthivaḥ
And worked up with joy your uncle Sugriva, the lord of earth and monkeys, said “Send them all here speedily."

श्रुत्वा दधिमुखस्यैतद्वचनं श्लक्ष्णमङ्गदः
अब्रवीत्तान्हरिश्रेष्ठो वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः

śrutvā dadhimukhasyaitadvacanaṁ ślakṣṇamaṅgadaḥ
abravīttānhariśreṣṭho vākyaṁ vākyaviśāradaḥ
Hearing those words from Dadhimukha, Angada, the foremost of the monkeys and skilled in speech, addressed them all, saying.

शङ्के श्रुतोऽयं वृत्तान्तो रामेण हरियूथपाः
तत्क्षमं नेह नः स्थातुं कृते कार्ये परंतपाः

śaṅke śruto'yaṁ vṛttānto rāmeṇa hariyūthapāḥ
tatkṣamaṁ neha naḥ sthātuṁ kṛte kārye paraṁtapāḥ

O you leaders of the monkey hosts, I fear, Rama has heard all about this. Dadhimukha relates everything joyfully and hence I infer this. And our work finished, O slayer of foes, it dose not behove us to remain here (any longer).

पीत्वा मधु यथाकामं विश्रान्ता वनचारिणः
किं शेषं गमनं तत्र सुग्रीवो यत्र मे गुरुः

pītvā madhu yathākāmaṁ viśrāntā vanacāriṇaḥ
kiṁ śeṣaṁ gamanaṁ tatra sugrīvo yatra me guruḥ
You have all drunk honey at your pleasure and there is nothing left and you should now go where the monkey king Sugriva is.

सर्वे यथा मां वक्ष्यन्ति समेत्य हरियूथपाः
तथास्मि कर्ता कर्तव्ये भवद्भिः परवानहम्

sarve yathā māṁ vakṣyanti sametya hariyūthapāḥ
tathāsmi kartā kartavye bhavadbhiḥ paravānaham
O leading monkeys, I shall follow what you will in a band desire me to do. In action I am subordinate to you all.

नाज्ञापयितुमीशोऽहं युवराजोऽस्मि यद्यपि
अयुक्तं कृतकर्माणो यूयं धर्षयितुं मया

nājñāpayitumīśo'haṁ yuvarājo'smi yadyapi
ayuktaṁ kṛtakarmāṇo yūyaṁ dharṣayituṁ mayā
I am not justified to command although I am a prince. You are all of accomplished actions, it is not proper to repress you forcibly.

ब्रुवतश्चाङ्गदश्चैवं श्रुत्वा वचनमव्ययम्
प्रहृष्टमनसो वाक्यमिदमूचुर्वनौकसः

bruvataścāṅgadaścaivaṁ śrutvā vacanamavyayam
prahṛṣṭamanaso vākyamidamūcurvanaukasaḥ
Hearing those sweet words of the prince Angada, the monkeys delightedly replied, saying.

एवं वक्ष्यति को राजन्प्रभुः सन्वानरर्षभ
ऐश्वर्यमदमत्तो हि सर्वोऽहमिति मन्यते

evaṁ vakṣyati ko rājanprabhuḥ sanvānararṣabha
aiśvaryamadamatto hi sarvo'hamiti manyate
O king, O foremost of monkeys, who else can speak thus being a master? Any one else, we think, is proud of his wealth.

तव चेदं सुसदृशं वाक्यं नान्यस्य कस्यचित्
संनतिर्हि तवाख्याति भविष्यच्छुभभाग्यताम्

tava cedaṁ susadṛśaṁ vākyaṁ nānyasya kasyacit
saṁnatirhi tavākhyāti bhaviṣyacchubhabhāgyatām
Such like words become you only and none else. Your humility speaks of your future greatness.

सर्वे वयमपि प्राप्तास्तत्र गन्तुं कृतक्षणाः
स यत्र हरिवीराणां सुग्रीवः पतिरव्ययः

sarve vayamapi prāptāstatra gantuṁ kṛtakṣaṇāḥ
sa yatra harivīrāṇāṁ sugrīvaḥ patiravyayaḥ
We are all anxious to go there, where Sugriva, the king of the monkeys, is.

त्वया ह्यनुक्तैर्हरिभिर्नैव शक्यं पदात्पदम्
क्वचिद्गन्तुं हरिश्रेष्ठ ब्रूमः सत्यमिदं तु ते

tvayā hyanuktairharibhirnaiva śakyaṁ padātpadam
kvacidgantuṁ hariśreṣṭha brūmaḥ satyamidaṁ tu te
Verily we speak to you, O foremost of monkeys, that without your permission, none among us, is capable of advancing a single step.”

उत्पतन्तमनूत्पेतुः सर्वे ते हरियूथपाः
कृत्वाकाशं निराकाशं यज्ञोत्क्षिप्ता इवानलाः

utpatantamanūtpetuḥ sarve te hariyūthapāḥ
kṛtvākāśaṁ nirākāśaṁ yajñotkṣiptā ivānalāḥ

They addressing him thus, Angada replied"All right, let us all go.” Saying this he leaped up in the sky and was followed by all those monkeys, clouding the welkin as if with stones thrown up by a tool.

तेऽम्बरं सहसोत्पत्य वेगवन्तः प्लवंगमाः
विनदन्तो महानादं घना वातेरिता यथा

te'mbaraṁ sahasotpatya vegavantaḥ plavaṁgamāḥ
vinadanto mahānādaṁ ghanā vāteritā yathā
And placing before them Angada and Hanuman, the monkeys leaping vehemently up in the sky roared like to clouds driven by the wind.

अङ्गदे ह्यननुप्राप्ते सुग्रीवो वानराधिपः
उवाच शोकोपहतं रामं कमललोचनम्

aṅgade hyananuprāpte sugrīvo vānarādhipaḥ
uvāca śokopahataṁ rāmaṁ kamalalocanam
And Angada nearing, Sugriva, the lord of the monkeys, spoke to the lotus-eyed Rama, stricken with grief, saying.

समाश्वसिहि भद्रं ते दृष्टा देवी न संशयः
नागन्तुमिह शक्यं तैरतीते समये हि नः

samāśvasihi bhadraṁ te dṛṣṭā devī na saṁśayaḥ
nāgantumiha śakyaṁ tairatīte samaye hi naḥ
May good betide you. Do you console yourself. The worshipful dame has been found out; there is not the least doubt about it. Or else they would not have come as the time is already past.

न मत्सकाशमागच्छेत्कृत्ये हि विनिपातिते
युवराजो महाबाहुः प्लवतां प्रवरोऽङ्गदः

na matsakāśamāgacchetkṛtye hi vinipātite
yuvarājo mahābāhuḥ plavatāṁ pravaro'ṅgadaḥ

I (further more) infer this from Angada's joy, O you of auspicious presence. Without being successful in his mission, the large-armed prince, Angada, the foremost of the monkeys, would not have come to me.

यद्यप्यकृतकृत्यानामीदृशः स्यादुपक्रमः
भवेत्तु दीनवदनो भ्रान्तविप्लुतमानसः

yadyapyakṛtakṛtyānāmīdṛśaḥ syādupakramaḥ
bhavettu dīnavadano bhrāntaviplutamānasaḥ

If the monkeys had engaged in such an unfair proceeding without being successful in their mission, Angada would have looked poorly and his mind would have been overwhelmed with grief and forgetfulness.

पितृपैतामहं चैतत्पूर्वकैरभिरक्षितम्
न मे मधुवनं हन्यादहृष्टः प्लवगेश्वरः

pitṛpaitāmahaṁ caitatpūrvakairabhirakṣitam
na me madhuvanaṁ hanyādahṛṣṭaḥ plavageśvaraḥ
Without beholding the daughter of the king Janaka they would not have dared to destroy Madhuvana obtained and preserved by my forefathers.

कौसल्या सुप्रजा राम समाश्वसिहि सुव्रत
दृष्टा देवी न संदेहो न चान्येन हनूमता
न ह्यन्यः कर्मणो हेतुः साधने तद्विधो भवेत्

kausalyā suprajā rāma samāśvasihi suvrata
dṛṣṭā devī na saṁdeho na cānyena hanūmatā
na hyanyaḥ karmaṇo hetuḥ sādhane tadvidho bhavet

Do you console yourself, O Rama, by whom Kausalya has become the mother of a good son. O you, rigidly observing any religious vow or obligation, forsooth has Hanuman behold the worshipful dame and none else.

जाम्बवान्यत्र नेता स्यादङ्गदश्च बलेश्वरः
हनूमांश्चाप्यधिष्ठाता न तस्य गतिरन्यथा

jāmbavānyatra netā syādaṅgadaśca baleśvaraḥ
hanūmāṁścāpyadhiṣṭhātā na tasya gatiranyathā
That work is sure to succeed whose leading spirits are the mighty Jambavana and Angada, and worker is Hanuman.

ततः किल किला शब्दं शुश्रावासन्नमम्बरे
हनूमत्कर्मदृप्तानां नर्दतां काननौकसाम्
किष्किन्धामुपयातानां सिद्धिं कथयतामिव

tataḥ kila kilā śabdaṁ śuśrāvāsannamambare
hanūmatkarmadṛptānāṁ nardatāṁ kānanaukasām
kiṣkindhāmupayātānāṁ siddhiṁ kathayatāmiva
Thereupon he heard in the sky the joyous sounds of the monkeys proud on account of Hanuman's work, proceeding towards Kiskindha and as if announcing their success.

ततः श्रुत्वा निनादं तं कपीनां कपिसत्तमः
आयताञ्चितलाङ्गूलः सोऽभवद्धृष्टमानसः

tataḥ śrutvā ninādaṁ taṁ kapīnāṁ kapisattamaḥ
āyatāñcitalāṅgūlaḥ so'bhavaddhṛṣṭamānasaḥ
Thereupon hearing the noise of these monkeys Sugriva, their chief, being greatly delighted, uplifted his tail.

आजग्मुस्तेऽपि हरयो रामदर्शनकाङ्क्षिणः
अङ्गदं पुरतः कृत्वा हनूमन्तं च वानरम्

ājagmuste'pi harayo rāmadarśanakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
aṅgadaṁ purataḥ kṛtvā hanūmantaṁ ca vānaram
And placing Angada and Hanuman before them those monkeys proceeded to behold Rama.

तेऽङ्गदप्रमुखा वीराः प्रहृष्टाश्च मुदान्विताः
निपेतुर्हरिराजस्य समीपे राघवस्य च

te'ṅgadapramukhā vīrāḥ prahṛṣṭāśca mudānvitāḥ
nipeturharirājasya samīpe rāghavasya ca
Those heroes headed by Angada, delighted and intoxicated, descended before Raghava and the lord of the monkeys.

हनूमांश्च महाबहुः प्रणम्य शिरसा ततः
नियतामक्षतां देवीं राघवाय न्यवेदयत्

hanūmāṁśca mahābahuḥ praṇamya śirasā tataḥ
niyatāmakṣatāṁ devīṁ rāghavāya nyavedayat
And the mighty-armed Hanuman, lowering his head, related to Raghava, Sita's spiritual and physical well-being.

निश्चितार्थं ततस्तस्मिन्सुग्रीवं पवनात्मजे
लक्ष्मणः प्रीतिमान्प्रीतं बहुमानादवैक्षत

niścitārthaṁ tatastasminsugrīvaṁ pavanātmaje
lakṣmaṇaḥ prītimānprītaṁ bahumānādavaikṣata
And being confirmed thus by the Wind-god's son, Laksmana, greatly pleased, respectfully looked towards Sugriva.

प्रीत्या च रममाणोऽथ राघवः परवीरहा
बहु मानेन महता हनूमन्तमवैक्षत

prītyā ca ramamāṇo'tha rāghavaḥ paravīrahā
bahu mānena mahatā hanūmantamavaikṣata
And Raghava too, the slayer of foes, worked up with joy, cast respectful looks towards Hanuman.

युवराजं पुरस्कृत्य सुग्रीवमभिवाद्य च
प्रवृत्तमथ सीतायाः प्रवक्तुमुपचक्रमुः

yuvarājaṁ puraskṛtya sugrīvamabhivādya ca
pravṛttamatha sītāyāḥ pravaktumupacakramuḥ

Thereupon getting at the Mount Prasravana surrounded by a variegated forest, lowering their heads to the mighty Rama and Laksmana, placing before them their prince (Angada) and bowing to Sugriva, the monkeys began to relate the story of Sita.

एतदाख्यान्ति ते सर्वे हरयो राम संनिधौ
वैदेहीमक्षतां श्रुत्वा रामस्तूत्तरमब्रवीत्

etadākhyānti te sarve harayo rāma saṁnidhau
vaidehīmakṣatāṁ śrutvā rāmastūttaramabravīt

And they described to Rama, the confinement of Sita in Ravana's seraglio, the remonstrances of the she-demons, her unflinching attachment in her lord and the time appointed (by the Raksasa for her destruction). And hearing of Vaidehi's well-being Rama said.

क्व सीता वर्तते देवी कथं च मयि वर्तते
एतन्मे सर्वमाख्यात वैदेहीं प्रति वानराः

kva sītā vartate devī kathaṁ ca mayi vartate
etanme sarvamākhyāta vaidehīṁ prati vānarāḥ
O monkeys where live the worshipful Sita? And how is her attachment to me? Do you relate everything to me.

रामस्य गदितं श्रुत्व हरयो रामसंनिधौ
चोदयन्ति हनूमन्तं सीतावृत्तान्तकोविदम्

rāmasya gaditaṁ śrutva harayo rāmasaṁnidhau
codayanti hanūmantaṁ sītāvṛttāntakovidam
Hearing those painful words of Rama, the monkeys desired Hanuman, conversant with the whereabouts of Sita, to describe every thing to him.

श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तेषां हनूमान्मारुतात्मजः
उवाच वाक्यं वाक्यज्ञः सीताया दर्शनं यथा

śrutvā tu vacanaṁ teṣāṁ hanūmānmārutātmajaḥ
uvāca vākyaṁ vākyajñaḥ sītāyā darśanaṁ yathā

Hearing their words, Hanuman, the Windgod's son, versed in the art of speech, lowering his head in Sita's name and towards the southern direction (where she lives) began to relate how he succeeded in beholding Sita.

दृष्टा मे राक्षसी मध्ये तर्ज्यमाना मुहुर्मुहुः
राक्षसीभिर्विरूपाभी रक्षिता प्रमदावने

dṛṣṭā me rākṣasī madhye tarjyamānā muhurmuhuḥ
rākṣasībhirvirūpābhī rakṣitā pramadāvane

And I saw there Sita, in the inner appartment of Ravana. Centring all her thoughts in you, breathes that damsel, O Rama. I saw her reviled by the she demons again and again. She is being guarded in that garden by the grim-visaged Raksasis.

दुःखमापद्यते देवी तवादुःखोचिता सती
रावणान्तःपुरे रुद्ध्वा राक्षसीभिः सुरक्षिता

duḥkhamāpadyate devī tavāduḥkhocitā satī
rāvaṇāntaḥpure ruddhvā rākṣasībhiḥ surakṣitā

And that worshipful came, O hero, ever used to happiness, is now stricken with grief in your absence. Confined in Ravana's inner apartment, well protected by those she-demons, wearing a single braid of hair and poorly, she is engaged only in thoughts touching you.

इक्ष्वाकुवंशविख्यातिं शनैः कीर्तयतानघ
स मया नरशार्दूल विश्वासमुपपादिता

ikṣvākuvaṁśavikhyātiṁ śanaiḥ kīrtayatānagha
sa mayā naraśārdūla viśvāsamupapāditā

O Kakutstha, O innocent prince, after enquiring for sometime, I found that worshipful dame devoted to you, and narrating the glories of the Iksvaku race, O foremost of men, I created her confidence by and by, and addressing her I related everything.

नियतः समुदाचारो भक्तिश्चास्यास्तथा त्वयि
एवं मया महाभागा दृष्टा जनकनन्दिनी
उग्रेण तपसा युक्ता त्वद्भक्त्या पुरुषर्षभ

niyataḥ samudācāro bhaktiścāsyāstathā tvayi
evaṁ mayā mahābhāgā dṛṣṭā janakanandinī
ugreṇa tapasā yuktā tvadbhaktyā puruṣarṣabha
O great man, O you best of men, I beheld the daughter of Janaka in this plight, engaged in hard austerities and ever devoted to you.

अभिज्ञानं च मे दत्तं यथावृत्तं तवान्तिके
चित्रकूटे महाप्राज्ञ वायसं प्रति राघव

abhijñānaṁ ca me dattaṁ yathāvṛttaṁ tavāntike
citrakūṭe mahāprājña vāyasaṁ prati rāghava
O you of great intelligence, O Raghava, offering me (this jewel) as a token, she wanted me to relate to you, the occurrence at the mount Citrakuta regarding the crow.

विज्ञाप्यश्च नर व्याघ्रो रामो वायुसुत त्वया
अखिलेनेह यद्दृष्टमिति मामाह जानकी

vijñāpyaśca nara vyāghro rāmo vāyusuta tvayā
akhileneha yaddṛṣṭamiti māmāha jānakī

And Janaki addressing me said'O Windgod's son, do you describe everything of what you have seen here, to Rama. And relating everything before Sugriva, do you present him with this jewel which has been preserved by me with great care.

एष निर्यातितः श्रीमान्मया ते वारिसंभवः
एतं दृष्ट्वा प्रमोदिष्ये व्यसने त्वामिवानघ

eṣa niryātitaḥ śrīmānmayā te vārisaṁbhavaḥ
etaṁ dṛṣṭvā pramodiṣye vyasane tvāmivānagha

I have kept with great care this excellent jewel of great effulgence. Do you remind him of the mark which he made on my forehead with red arsenic. O innocent monkey, greatly delighted am I on beholding the brilliant jewel which he has sent through you.

जीवितं धारयिष्यामि मासं दशरथात्मज
ऊर्ध्वं मासान्न जीवेयं रक्षसां वशमागता

jīvitaṁ dhārayiṣyāmi māsaṁ daśarathātmaja
ūrdhvaṁ māsānna jīveyaṁ rakṣasāṁ vaśamāgatā
Breathe shall I only for a month, beyond that I shall never live, subject as I am to the demons.'

इति मामब्रवीत्सीता कृशाङ्गी धर्म चारिणी
रावणान्तःपुरे रुद्धा मृगीवोत्फुल्ललोचना

iti māmabravītsītā kṛśāṅgī dharma cāriṇī
rāvaṇāntaḥpure ruddhā mṛgīvotphullalocanā
Thus was I accosted by Sita, reduced to a skeleton, observing pious observances, shut up in Ravana's inner apartment and having eyes like those of a hind.

एतदेव मयाख्यातं सर्वं राघव यद्यथा
सर्वथा सागरजले संतारः प्रविधीयताम्

etadeva mayākhyātaṁ sarvaṁ rāghava yadyathā
sarvathā sāgarajale saṁtāraḥ pravidhīyatām
I have described to you everything, O Raghava, do you make arrangements for bridging over the ocean.

तौ जाताश्वासौ राजपुत्रौ विदित्वा; तच्चाभिज्ञानं राघवाय प्रदाय
देव्या चाख्यातं सर्वमेवानुपूर्व्या;द्वाचा संपूर्णं वायुपुत्रः शशंस

tau jātāśvāsau rājaputrau viditvā; taccābhijñānaṁ rāghavāya pradāya
devyā cākhyātaṁ sarvamevānupūrvyā;dvācā saṁpūrṇaṁ vāyuputraḥ śaśaṁsa
And considering those two princes greatly consoled, the Wind-god's son handed over that token to Raghava and described everything from the beginning to the end.

एवमुक्तो हनुमता रामो दशरथात्मजः
तं मणिं हृदये कृत्वा प्ररुरोद सलक्ष्मणः

evamukto hanumatā rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ
taṁ maṇiṁ hṛdaye kṛtvā praruroda salakṣmaṇaḥ
Being thus accosted by Hanuman, Rama, the son of Dasaratha, placing that jewel on his breast, wept with Laksmana.

तं तु दृष्ट्वा मणिश्रेष्ठं राघवः शोककर्शितः
नेत्राभ्यामश्रुपूर्णाभ्यां सुग्रीवमिदमब्रवीत्

taṁ tu dṛṣṭvā maṇiśreṣṭhaṁ rāghavaḥ śokakarśitaḥ
netrābhyāmaśrupūrṇābhyāṁ sugrīvamidamabravīt
Beholding that excellent jewel, Raghava, stricken with grief, with eyes full of tears, spake to Sugriva, saying.

यथैव धेनुः स्रवति स्नेहाद्वत्सस्य वत्सला
तथा ममापि हृदयं मणिरत्नस्य दर्शनात्

yathaiva dhenuḥ sravati snehādvatsasya vatsalā
tathā mamāpi hṛdayaṁ maṇiratnasya darśanāt
Forsooth my heart melt on beholding this jewel as milk trickle down from the udders of a cow on beholding its calf.

मणिरत्नमिदं दत्तं वैदेह्याः श्वशुरेण मे
वधूकाले यथा बद्धमधिकं मूर्ध्नि शोभते

maṇiratnamidaṁ dattaṁ vaidehyāḥ śvaśureṇa me
vadhūkāle yathā baddhamadhikaṁ mūrdhni śobhate
This jewel was conferred on Sita by my father-in-law at the time of our wedding, and to enhance its beauty, she wore it on her head.

अयं हि जलसंभूतो मणिः प्रवरपूजितः
यज्ञे परमतुष्टेन दत्तः शक्रेण धीमता

ayaṁ hi jalasaṁbhūto maṇiḥ pravarapūjitaḥ
yajñe paramatuṣṭena dattaḥ śakreṇa dhīmatā
And this jewel, obtained from the bed of the ocean, was conferred on him (Janaka) by the intelligent Sakra, greatly delighted for being adored in a sacrifice.

इमं दृष्ट्वा मणिश्रेष्ठं तथा तातस्य दर्शनम्
अद्यास्म्यवगतः सौम्य वैदेहस्य तथा विभोः

imaṁ dṛṣṭvā maṇiśreṣṭhaṁ tathā tātasya darśanam
adyāsmyavagataḥ saumya vaidehasya tathā vibhoḥ
O gentle one, this bring back to my mind, the memory of my father, and father-in-law the king of Videha.

अयं हि शोभते तस्याः प्रियाया मूर्ध्नि मे मणिः
अद्यास्य दर्शनेनाहं प्राप्तां तामिव चिन्तये

ayaṁ hi śobhate tasyāḥ priyāyā mūrdhni me maṇiḥ
adyāsya darśanenāhaṁ prāptāṁ tāmiva cintaye
This excellent jewel appeared beautiful on the crown of my dear one, and methinks, on beholding it, I have as if got back my beloved spouse.

किमाह सीता वैदेही ब्रूहि सौम्य पुनः पुनः
परासुमिव तोयेन सिञ्चन्ती वाक्यवारिणा

kimāha sītā vaidehī brūhi saumya punaḥ punaḥ
parāsumiva toyena siñcantī vākyavāriṇā
Do you relate to me again and again, O gentle one what Vaidehi has said, as if sprinkling me with the water of her words like to one rendered senseless.

इतस्तु किं दुःखतरं यदिमं वारिसंभवम्
मणिं पश्यामि सौमित्रे वैदेहीमागतं विना

itastu kiṁ duḥkhataraṁ yadimaṁ vārisaṁbhavam
maṇiṁ paśyāmi saumitre vaidehīmāgataṁ vinā
What greater grief can there be, O Saumitri, that I behold the jewel obtained from the ocean but not Vaidehi.?

चिरं जीवति वैदेही यदि मासं धरिष्यति
क्षणं सौम्य न जीवेयं विना तामसितेक्षणाम्

ciraṁ jīvati vaidehī yadi māsaṁ dhariṣyati
kṣaṇaṁ saumya na jīveyaṁ vinā tāmasitekṣaṇām
Truly dose Vaidehi live for a long time if she breathes for a month. But O hero, I cannot live blue eyes.

नय मामपि तं देशं यत्र दृष्टा मम प्रिया
न तिष्ठेयं क्षणमपि प्रवृत्तिमुपलभ्य च

naya māmapi taṁ deśaṁ yatra dṛṣṭā mama priyā
na tiṣṭheyaṁ kṣaṇamapi pravṛttimupalabhya ca
Do you take me there where you had beheld iny dear spouse. I cannot live for a moment while I have received intelligence about her.

कथं सा मम सुश्रोणि भीरु भीरुः सती तदा
भयावहानां घोराणां मध्ये तिष्ठति रक्षसाम्

kathaṁ sā mama suśroṇi bhīru bhīruḥ satī tadā
bhayāvahānāṁ ghorāṇāṁ madhye tiṣṭhati rakṣasām
How live that timid damsel, having a beautiful waist, being terrified, amidst the terrible and grim Raksasis?

शारदस्तिमिरोन्मुखो नूनं चन्द्र इवाम्बुदैः
आवृतं वदनं तस्या न विराजति राक्षसैः

śāradastimironmukho nūnaṁ candra ivāmbudaiḥ
āvṛtaṁ vadanaṁ tasyā na virājati rākṣasaiḥ
Truly her countenance is not appearing beautiful like to the autumnal moon, enveloped with clouds, although cleared off the darkness.

किमाह सीता हनुमंस्तत्त्वतः कथयस्व मे
एतेन खलु जीविष्ये भेषजेनातुरो यथा

kimāha sītā hanumaṁstattvataḥ kathayasva me
etena khalu jīviṣye bheṣajenāturo yathā
Do you relate to me in sooth, O Hanuman, what Sita has spoken to you. I shall live by these words, as the sick are cured by medicine.

मधुरा मधुरालापा किमाह मम भामिनी
मद्विहीना वरारोहा हनुमन्कथयस्व मे
दुःखाद्दुःखतरं प्राप्य कथं जीवति जानकी

madhurā madhurālāpā kimāha mama bhāminī
madvihīnā varārohā hanumankathayasva me
duḥkhādduḥkhataraṁ prāpya kathaṁ jīvati jānakī
O Hanuman, what has my dear wife, sweetspeeched, and highly beautiful, spoken to you, being separated form me? How breathes she going through a series of calamities?

एवमुक्तस्तु हनुमान्राघवेण महात्मना
सीताया भाषितं सर्वं न्यवेदयत राघवे

evamuktastu hanumānrāghaveṇa mahātmanā
sītāyā bhāṣitaṁ sarvaṁ nyavedayata rāghave
Being thus addressed by the high-souled Raghava, Hanuman, related to him all of what Sita had said,

इदमुक्तवती देवी जानकी पुरुषर्षभ
पूर्ववृत्तमभिज्ञानं चित्रकूटे यथा तथम्

idamuktavatī devī jānakī puruṣarṣabha
pūrvavṛttamabhijñānaṁ citrakūṭe yathā tatham
O foremost of men, the worshipful Janaki, related as a token, all the incidents at the Mount Citrakuta from the beginning to the end.

सुखसुप्ता त्वया सार्धं जानकी पूर्वमुत्थिता
वायसः सहसोत्पत्य विरराद स्तनान्तरे

sukhasuptā tvayā sārdhaṁ jānakī pūrvamutthitā
vāyasaḥ sahasotpatya virarāda stanāntare
Sleeping happily with you, Janaki one day awoke before, and in the meantime, a crow wounded her breast with its beaks.

पर्यायेण च सुप्तस्त्वं देव्यङ्के भरताग्रज
पुनश्च किल पक्षी स देव्या जनयति व्यथाम्

paryāyeṇa ca suptastvaṁ devyaṅke bharatāgraja
punaśca kila pakṣī sa devyā janayati vyathām
O Rama, you wert then asleep on Sita's lap and that crow again afflicted the worshipful dame.

वायसेन च तेनैव सततं बाध्यमानया
बोधितः किल देव्यास्त्वं सुखसुप्तः परंतप

vāyasena ca tenaiva satataṁ bādhyamānayā
bodhitaḥ kila devyāstvaṁ sukhasuptaḥ paraṁtapa
And it again wounded her. And being bathed in blood and suffering terrible pangs, that worshipful dame aroused you.

तां तु दृष्ट्वा महाबाहो रादितां च स्तनान्तरे
आशीविष इव क्रुद्धो निःश्वसन्नभ्यभाषथाः

tāṁ tu dṛṣṭvā mahābāho rāditāṁ ca stanāntare
āśīviṣa iva kruddho niḥśvasannabhyabhāṣathāḥ
O slayer of foes, O you of mighty-arms, seeing her breast wounded, you, wroth like a serpent, didst speak saying.

नखाग्रैः केन ते भीरु दारितं तु स्तनान्तरम्
कः क्रीडति सरोषेण पञ्चवक्त्रेण भोगिना

nakhāgraiḥ kena te bhīru dāritaṁ tu stanāntaram
kaḥ krīḍati saroṣeṇa pañcavaktreṇa bhoginā
O timid damsel, who, with his nails, has wounded your breast? Who has played with an angry serpent having five faces?

निरीक्षमाणः सहसा वायसं समवैक्षताः
नखैः सरुधिरैस्तीक्ष्णैर्मामेवाभिमुखं स्थितम्

nirīkṣamāṇaḥ sahasā vāyasaṁ samavaikṣatāḥ
nakhaiḥ sarudhiraistīkṣṇairmāmevābhimukhaṁ sthitam
Casting your looks around you didst behold a crow facing the worshipful dame with sharpened nails besmeared with blood.

सुतः किल स शक्रस्य वायसः पततां वरः
धरान्तरचरः शीघ्रं पवनस्य गतौ समः

sutaḥ kila sa śakrasya vāyasaḥ patatāṁ varaḥ
dharāntaracaraḥ śīghraṁ pavanasya gatau samaḥ
That crow, the best of the birds, was Sakra's son. And it entered speedily into the earth with the velocity of the wind,

ततस्तस्मिन्महाबाहो कोपसंवर्तितेक्षणः
वायसे त्वं कृत्वाः क्रूरां मतिं मतिमतां वर

tatastasminmahābāho kopasaṁvartitekṣaṇaḥ
vāyase tvaṁ kṛtvāḥ krūrāṁ matiṁ matimatāṁ vara
Thereupon, your eyes rolling with ire, you, O mighty armed hero, O foremost of the intelligent, did resolve to destroy that crow.

स दर्भं संस्तराद्गृह्य ब्रह्मास्त्रेण न्ययोजयः
स दीप्त इव कालाग्निर्जज्वालाभिमुखः खगम्

sa darbhaṁ saṁstarādgṛhya brahmāstreṇa nyayojayaḥ
sa dīpta iva kālāgnirjajvālābhimukhaḥ khagam
Taking a kusa off your seat you did set it on Brahma weapon. And it flamed like to the fire of desolation before that crow.

स त्वं प्रदीप्तं चिक्षेप दर्भं तं वायसं प्रति
ततस्तु वायसं दीप्तः स दर्भोऽनुजगाम ह

sa tvaṁ pradīptaṁ cikṣepa darbhaṁ taṁ vāyasaṁ prati
tatastu vāyasaṁ dīptaḥ sa darbho'nujagāma ha
You did let off that burning Kusa towards that birds. And there upon that burning Kuca followed the crow.

स पित्रा च परित्यक्तः सुरैः सर्वैर्महर्षिभिः
त्रीँल्लोकान्संपरिक्रम्य त्रातारं नाधिगच्छति

sa pitrā ca parityaktaḥ suraiḥ sarvairmaharṣibhiḥ
trī̐llokānsaṁparikramya trātāraṁ nādhigacchati
And being forsaken even by the celestials, who were terrified, and ransacking the three worlds it did not get a refuge.

तं त्वं निपतितं भूमौ शरण्यः शरणागतम्
वधार्हमपि काकुत्स्थ कृपया परिपालयः

taṁ tvaṁ nipatitaṁ bhūmau śaraṇyaḥ śaraṇāgatam
vadhārhamapi kākutstha kṛpayā paripālayaḥ
And, placing himself on the earth, he sought his shelter, and Kakutstha, out of mercy, saved him, albeit worthy of being killed.

मोघमस्त्रं न शक्यं तु कर्तुमित्येव राघव
ततस्तस्याक्षिकाकस्य हिनस्ति स्म स दक्षिणम्

moghamastraṁ na śakyaṁ tu kartumityeva rāghava
tatastasyākṣikākasya hinasti sma sa dakṣiṇam
And thinking if improper to baffle the aim of the weapon, you didst, O Raghava, destroy the right eye of the crow.

राम त्वां स नमस्कृत्वा राज्ञो दशरथस्य च
विसृष्टस्तु तदा काकः प्रतिपेदे खमालयम्

rāma tvāṁ sa namaskṛtvā rājño daśarathasya ca
visṛṣṭastu tadā kākaḥ pratipede khamālayam
Thereupon bowing to you and the king Dasaratha, that crow, bidding adieu, went to its quarter.

एवमस्त्रविदां श्रेष्ठः सत्त्ववाञ्शीलवानपि
किमर्थमस्त्रं रक्षःसु न योजयसि राघव

evamastravidāṁ śreṣṭhaḥ sattvavāñśīlavānapi
kimarthamastraṁ rakṣaḥsu na yojayasi rāghava
O Raghava, you are the foremost of those skilled in the use of weapons, powerful and gifted with an excellent character, why do you not discharge weapons towards the Raksasas?

न नागा नापि गन्धर्वा नासुरा न मरुद्गणाः
तव राम मुखे स्थातुं शक्ताः प्रतिसमाधितुम्

na nāgā nāpi gandharvā nāsurā na marudgaṇāḥ
tava rāma mukhe sthātuṁ śaktāḥ pratisamādhitum
The celestials, the Gandharvas, the Asuras, the Marutas-none of them is qualified, O Rama, to equal you in conflict.

तव वीर्यवतः कच्चिन्मयि यद्यस्ति संभ्रमः
क्षिप्रं सुनिशितैर्बाणैर्हन्यतां युधि रावणः

tava vīryavataḥ kaccinmayi yadyasti saṁbhramaḥ
kṣipraṁ suniśitairbāṇairhanyatāṁ yudhi rāvaṇaḥ
If you, gifted with great prowess, had any armed shafts, destroy Ravana in conflict.

भ्रातुरादेशमादाय लक्ष्मणो वा परंतपः
स किमर्थं नरवरो न मां रक्षति राघवः

bhrāturādeśamādāya lakṣmaṇo vā paraṁtapaḥ
sa kimarthaṁ naravaro na māṁ rakṣati rāghavaḥ
And obtaining the behests of his brother, why dose not Laksmana, the subduer of foes and best of men, protect me, O Raghava?

शक्तौ तौ पुरुषव्याघ्रौ वाय्वग्निसमतेजसौ
सुराणामपि दुर्धर्षौ किमर्थं मामुपेक्षतः

śaktau tau puruṣavyāghrau vāyvagnisamatejasau
surāṇāmapi durdharṣau kimarthaṁ māmupekṣataḥ
Those two best of men, gifted with the effulgence of Wind and Fire, and incapable of being repressed even by the celestials, are disregarding me.

ममैव दुष्कृतं किंचिन्महदस्ति न संशयः
समर्थौ सहितौ यन्मां नापेक्षेते परंतपौ

mamaiva duṣkṛtaṁ kiṁcinmahadasti na saṁśayaḥ
samarthau sahitau yanmāṁ nāpekṣete paraṁtapau
Forsooth have I perpetrated a mighty iniquity since those two slayers of foes, being capable, do not protect me.

त्वच्छोकविमुखो रामो देवि सत्येन ते शपे
रामे दुःखाभिभूते च लक्ष्मणः परितप्यते

tvacchokavimukho rāmo devi satyena te śape
rāme duḥkhābhibhūte ca lakṣmaṇaḥ paritapyate
O exalted one, I swear by truth, Rama turn away he countenance (from every work) in consequence of grief for you. And Rama being seized with sorrow, Laksmana burns in grief.

कथंचिद्भवती दृष्टा न कालः परिशोचितुम्
इमं मुहूर्तं दुःखानामन्तं द्रक्ष्यसि भामिनि

kathaṁcidbhavatī dṛṣṭā na kālaḥ pariśocitum
imaṁ muhūrtaṁ duḥkhānāmantaṁ drakṣyasi bhāmini
It dose not behove you to relent any more as I have succeeded in finding you out. You shall at this very moment behold the end of your grief.

तावुभौ नरशार्दूलौ राजपुत्रावरिंदमौ
त्वद्दर्शनकृतोत्साहौ लङ्कां भस्मीकरिष्यतः

tāvubhau naraśārdūlau rājaputrāvariṁdamau
tvaddarśanakṛtotsāhau laṅkāṁ bhasmīkariṣyataḥ
And those two princes, the foremost of men and slayers of foes, actuated with energy on hearing that I have seen you, shall reduce Lanka to ashes.

हत्वा च समरे रौद्रं रावणं सह बान्धवम्
राघवस्त्वां महाबाहुः स्वां पुरीं नयते ध्रुवम्

hatvā ca samare raudraṁ rāvaṇaṁ saha bāndhavam
rāghavastvāṁ mahābāhuḥ svāṁ purīṁ nayate dhruvam
And slaying in conflict the terrible Ravana, with his kith and kin, Raghava, in sooth, O excellent damsel, shall take you back to his own city.

यत्तु रामो विजानीयादभिज्ञानमनिन्दिते
प्रीतिसंजननं तस्य प्रदातुं तत्त्वमर्हसि

yattu rāmo vijānīyādabhijñānamanindite
prītisaṁjananaṁ tasya pradātuṁ tattvamarhasi
O you of a blameless person, do you confer on me such a token, as might be recognized by Rama and conduce to his pleasure.

साभिवीक्ष्य दिशः सर्वा वेण्युद्ग्रथनमुत्तमम्
मुक्त्वा वस्त्राद्ददौ मह्यं मणिमेतं महाबल

sābhivīkṣya diśaḥ sarvā veṇyudgrathanamuttamam
muktvā vastrāddadau mahyaṁ maṇimetaṁ mahābala
Thereat, casting her looks around, she took out an excellent jewel from her cloth, worthy of being set on her braid and conferred it on me, O you of great strength.

प्रतिगृह्य मणिं दिव्यं तव हेतो रघूत्तम
शिरसा संप्रणम्यैनामहमागमने त्वरे

pratigṛhya maṇiṁ divyaṁ tava heto raghūttama
śirasā saṁpraṇamyaināmahamāgamane tvare
O you, the most favourite of the Raghu race, taking for you that gem with my hands and bowing to her, I addressed myself speedily for departure.

गमने च कृतोत्साहमवेक्ष्य वरवर्णिनी
विवर्धमानं च हि मामुवाच जनकात्मजा
अश्रुपूर्णमुखी दीना बाष्पसंदिग्धभाषिणी

gamane ca kṛtotsāhamavekṣya varavarṇinī
vivardhamānaṁ ca hi māmuvāca janakātmajā
aśrupūrṇamukhī dīnā bāṣpasaṁdigdhabhāṣiṇī

Thereupon beholding me ready to depart and increase in bulk and about to leap up in the welkin, Sita, the daughter of the king Janaka, poorly, bathed in tears, overwhelmed with sorrow and having her voice choked with grief, saying 'Blessed are you O great monkey, since you shall behold the large-armed and the lotuseyed Rama and the highly famed Laksmana, my lord's younger brother.

हनुमन्सिंहसंकाशौ तावुभौ रामलक्ष्मणौ
सुग्रीवं च सहामात्यं सर्वान्ब्रूया अनामयम्

hanumansiṁhasaṁkāśau tāvubhau rāmalakṣmaṇau
sugrīvaṁ ca sahāmātyaṁ sarvānbrūyā anāmayam
Addressing me with these words she again said-O Hanuman, do you relate my well-being to Rama and Lakshamana of leonine prowess, and Sugriva accompanied by his followers.

यथा च स महाबाहुर्मां तारयति राघवः
अस्माद्दुःखाम्बुसंरोधात्तत्समाधातुमर्हसि

yathā ca sa mahābāhurmāṁ tārayati rāghavaḥ
asmādduḥkhāmbusaṁrodhāttatsamādhātumarhasi
Do you so describe as the large-armed Raghava may save me from this ocean of grief.

इमं च तीव्रं मम शोकवेगं; रक्षोभिरेभिः परिभर्त्सनं च
ब्रूयास्तु रामस्य गतः समीपं; शिवश्च तेऽध्वास्तु हरिप्रवीर

imaṁ ca tīvraṁ mama śokavegaṁ; rakṣobhirebhiḥ paribhartsanaṁ ca
brūyāstu rāmasya gataḥ samīpaṁ; śivaśca te'dhvāstu haripravīra
Do you narrate to Rama this my terrible sorrow and the affliction by the she-demons. May good betide you, on your way, O foremost of the monkeys.'

एतत्तवार्या नृपराजसिंह; सीता वचः प्राह विषादपूर्वम्
एतच्च बुद्ध्वा गदितं मया त्वं; श्रद्धत्स्व सीतां कुशलां समग्राम्

etattavāryā nṛparājasiṁha; sītā vacaḥ prāha viṣādapūrvam
etacca buddhvā gaditaṁ mayā tvaṁ; śraddhatsva sītāṁ kuśalāṁ samagrām
Thus the worshipful Sita gave vent to these piteous accents. Hearing these words do you believe that it is all well with her.

अथाहमुत्तरं देव्या पुनरुक्तः ससंभ्रमम्
तव स्नेहान्नरव्याघ्र सौहार्यादनुमान्य च

athāhamuttaraṁ devyā punaruktaḥ sasaṁbhramam
tava snehānnaravyāghra sauhāryādanumānya ca
Thereupon, O foremost of men, out of your love and adoring me for your friendship, that worshipful dame-addressed me again, saying.

एवं बहुविधं वाच्यो रामो दाशरथिस्त्वया
यथा मामाप्नुयाच्छीघ्रं हत्वा रावणमाहवे

evaṁ bahuvidhaṁ vācyo rāmo dāśarathistvayā
yathā māmāpnuyācchīghraṁ hatvā rāvaṇamāhave
Do you thus speak every thing to Rama, the son of Dasaratha, so that he might soon take me hence, slaying Ravana in battle.

यदि वा मन्यसे वीर वसैकाहमरिंदम
कस्मिंश्चित्संवृते देशे विश्रान्तः श्वो गमिष्यसि

yadi vā manyase vīra vasaikāhamariṁdama
kasmiṁścitsaṁvṛte deśe viśrāntaḥ śvo gamiṣyasi
O hero, O slayer of foes, if it please you, you may relieve yourself of the toil by living in a secret nook and then proceed to-morrow.

मम चाप्यल्पभाग्यायाः साम्निध्यात्तव वानर
अस्य शोकविपाकस्य मुहूर्तं स्याद्विमोक्षणम्

mama cāpyalpabhāgyāyāḥ sāmnidhyāttava vānara
asya śokavipākasya muhūrtaṁ syādvimokṣaṇam
O monkey, in your company, I do momentarily forget the weight of my grief, unfortunate as I am.

गते हि त्वयि विक्रान्ते पुनरागमनाय वै
प्राणानामपि संदेहो मम स्यान्नात्र संशयः

gate hi tvayi vikrānte punarāgamanāya vai
prāṇānāmapi saṁdeho mama syānnātra saṁśayaḥ
O you gifted with great prowess, yourself departing, I shall wait for your return, but doubt I very much whether I shall live till then.

तवादर्शनजः शोको भूयो मां परितापयेत्
दुःखाद्दुःखपराभूतां दुर्गतां दुःखभागिनीम्

tavādarśanajaḥ śoko bhūyo māṁ paritāpayet
duḥkhādduḥkhaparābhūtāṁ durgatāṁ duḥkhabhāginīm
Burnt I shall be with the fear of not beholding you again, wretched and stricken with grief as I am. And so I shall be, hereafter, overwhelmed with a mightier grief.

त्रयाणामेव भूतानां सागरस्यास्य लङ्घने
शक्तिः स्याद्वैनतेयस्य वायोर्वा तव वानघ

trayāṇāmeva bhūtānāṁ sāgarasyāsya laṅghane
śaktiḥ syādvainateyasya vāyorvā tava vānagha
O innocent monkey of all the creatures three only are qualified to cross over the ocean, yourself, Garuda and the Wind.

तदस्मिन्कार्यनियोगे वीरैवं दुरतिक्रमे
किं पश्यसि समाधानं ब्रूहि कार्यविदां वर

tadasminkāryaniyoge vīraivaṁ duratikrame
kiṁ paśyasi samādhānaṁ brūhi kāryavidāṁ vara
O you foremost of those skilled in speech, what had you settled about the accomplishment of this hard work?

काममस्य त्वमेवैकः कार्यस्य परिसाधने
पर्याप्तः परवीरघ्न यशस्यस्ते बलोदयः

kāmamasya tvamevaikaḥ kāryasya parisādhane
paryāptaḥ paravīraghna yaśasyaste balodayaḥ
Or you alone, O destroyer of hostile heroes, are quite enough for the fulfilment of this purpose; and you shall reap, in the shape of fame, the fruit of your achievement.

बलैः समग्रैर्यदि मां हत्वा रावणमाहवे
विजयी स्वां पुरीं रामो नयेत्तत्स्याद्यशस्करम्

balaiḥ samagrairyadi māṁ hatvā rāvaṇamāhave
vijayī svāṁ purīṁ rāmo nayettatsyādyaśaskaram
But if Rama, obtaining victory, can take me hence to his own city, it shall redound to his glory.

यथाहं तस्य वीरस्य वनादुपधिना हृता
रक्षसा तद्भयादेव तथा नार्हति राघवः

yathāhaṁ tasya vīrasya vanādupadhinā hṛtā
rakṣasā tadbhayādeva tathā nārhati rāghavaḥ
It dose not behove the heroic Raghava, to take me away by steal, like to Ravana capturing me from the forest under a disguise.

बलैस्तु संकुलां कृत्वा लङ्कां परबलार्दनः
मां नयेद्यदि काकुत्स्थस्तत्तस्य सदृशं भवेत्

balaistu saṁkulāṁ kṛtvā laṅkāṁ parabalārdanaḥ
māṁ nayedyadi kākutsthastattasya sadṛśaṁ bhavet
But if blocking up Lanka with his forces, that afflictor of enemies, Kakutstha, take me (from hence), then that shall be worthy of him.

तद्यथा तस्य विक्रान्तमनुरूपं महात्मनः
भवत्याहवशूरस्य तथा त्वमुपपादय

tadyathā tasya vikrāntamanurūpaṁ mahātmanaḥ
bhavatyāhavaśūrasya tathā tvamupapādaya
Therefore do you so order things that powerful and high-souled hero in conflict, may act as becomes himself.

तदर्थोपहितं वाक्यं प्रश्रितं हेतुसंहितम्
निशम्याहं ततः शेषं वाक्यमुत्तरमब्रुवम्

tadarthopahitaṁ vākyaṁ praśritaṁ hetusaṁhitam
niśamyāhaṁ tataḥ śeṣaṁ vākyamuttaramabruvam
Hearing these sound reasonable and affectionate words I gave her the last reply, saying.

देवि हर्यृक्षसैन्यानामीश्वरः प्लवतां वरः
सुग्रीवः सत्त्वसंपन्नस्तवार्थे कृतनिश्चयः

devi haryṛkṣasainyānāmīśvaraḥ plavatāṁ varaḥ
sugrīvaḥ sattvasaṁpannastavārthe kṛtaniścayaḥ
O revered lady, that foremost of monkeysthe lord of bears and monkeys-Sugriva, possessed of truth, has made up his mind on your behalf.

येषां नोपरि नाधस्तान्न तिर्यक्सज्जते गतिः
न च कर्मसु सीदन्ति महत्स्वमिततेजसः

yeṣāṁ nopari nādhastānna tiryaksajjate gatiḥ
na ca karmasu sīdanti mahatsvamitatejasaḥ

And exceedingly powerful and mighty monkeys possessed of prowess, and speeding far with the rapidity of thought, are in his command. Nothing can impede their courses, either upward, or downward, or tending in both directions, and those ones of measureless energy never experience depression in the most arduous undertakings.

असकृत्तैर्महाभागैर्वानरैर्बलसंयुतैः
प्रदक्षिणीकृता भूमिर्वायुमार्गानुसारिभिः

asakṛttairmahābhāgairvānarairbalasaṁyutaiḥ
pradakṣiṇīkṛtā bhūmirvāyumārgānusāribhiḥ
And those great and powerful monkeys, coursing in the air, have again and again circumambulated the earth.

मद्विशिष्टाश्च तुल्याश्च सन्ति तत्र वनौकसः
मत्तः प्रत्यवरः कश्चिन्नास्ति सुग्रीवसंनिधौ

madviśiṣṭāśca tulyāśca santi tatra vanaukasaḥ
mattaḥ pratyavaraḥ kaścinnāsti sugrīvasaṁnidhau
Sugriva has many monkeys-my equal-and greater than I but none of inferior strength.

अहं तावदिह प्राप्तः किं पुनस्ते महाबलाः
न हि प्रकृष्टाः प्रेष्यन्ते प्रेष्यन्ते हीतरे जनाः

ahaṁ tāvadiha prāptaḥ kiṁ punaste mahābalāḥ
na hi prakṛṣṭāḥ preṣyante preṣyante hītare janāḥ
While I have crossed over the main-what of these mighty heroes? The leading heroes are never sent on a mission but only those of inferior merit.

तदलं परितापेन देवि मन्युर्व्यपैतु ते
एकोत्पातेन ते लङ्कामेष्यन्ति हरियूथपाः

tadalaṁ paritāpena devi manyurvyapaitu te
ekotpātena te laṅkāmeṣyanti hariyūthapāḥ
No more of bewailing, O worshipful dame. Do you remove your grief. And with one leap these leaders of monkey-hosts shall reach Lanka.

मम पृष्ठगतौ तौ च चन्द्रसूर्याविवोदितौ
त्वत्सकाशं महाभागे नृसिंहावागमिष्यतः

mama pṛṣṭhagatau tau ca candrasūryāvivoditau
tvatsakāśaṁ mahābhāge nṛsiṁhāvāgamiṣyataḥ
O great damsel, these two princes, placing themselves on my back shall come to you like to the rising Sun and Moon.

अरिघ्नं सिंहसंकाशं क्षिप्रं द्रक्ष्यसि राघवम्
लक्ष्मणं च धनुष्पाणिं लङ्का द्वारमुपस्थितम्

arighnaṁ siṁhasaṁkāśaṁ kṣipraṁ drakṣyasi rāghavam
lakṣmaṇaṁ ca dhanuṣpāṇiṁ laṅkā dvāramupasthitam
You shall soon behold before Lanka's gate Raghava the slayer of foes resembling a lion and Laksmana with a bow in his hand.

नखदंष्ट्रायुधान्वीरान्सिंहशार्दूलविक्रमान्
वानरान्वानरेन्द्राभान्क्षिप्रं द्रक्ष्यसि संगतान्

nakhadaṁṣṭrāyudhānvīrānsiṁhaśārdūlavikramān
vānarānvānarendrābhānkṣipraṁ drakṣyasi saṁgatān
You shall soon observe in a band the heroic monkeys, gifted with the strength of lions and tigers, and having nails and teeth for their weapons.

शैलाम्बुदन्निकाशानां लङ्कामलयसानुषु
नर्दतां कपिमुख्यानामचिराच्छोष्यसे स्वनम्

śailāmbudannikāśānāṁ laṅkāmalayasānuṣu
nardatāṁ kapimukhyānāmacirācchoṣyase svanam
You shall soon bear the roaring of the leading monkeys on the summit of mount Malaya, resembling the muttering of the clouds.

निवृत्तवनवासं च त्वया सार्धमरिंदमम्
अभिषिक्तमयोध्यायां क्षिप्रं द्रक्ष्यसि राघवम्

nivṛttavanavāsaṁ ca tvayā sārdhamariṁdamam
abhiṣiktamayodhyāyāṁ kṣipraṁ drakṣyasi rāghavam
You shall soon behold Raghava, the slayer of foes, installed along with you on the throne of Ayodhya after returning from the forest.

ततो मया वाग्भिरदीनभाषिणी; शिवाभिरिष्टाभिरभिप्रसादिता
जगाम शान्तिं मम मैथिलात्मजा; तवापि शोकेन तथाभिपीडिता

tato mayā vāgbhiradīnabhāṣiṇī; śivābhiriṣṭābhirabhiprasāditā
jagāma śāntiṁ mama maithilātmajā; tavāpi śokena tathābhipīḍitā
That daughter of the king of Mithila although heavily laden with sorrow in your absence was greatly comforted and pleased by my auspicious words boding the fulfilment of her desire.
